1	"""`snap_sync`: snap name/channel/revision convergence through snapd's own verbs
2	(D-06, D-14, D-29, ADR-020).
3	
4	WARNING — `snap refresh --hold` with NO snap name is a MUTATING command: called that
5	way it silently sets an INDEFINITE GLOBAL hold on auto-refresh for every snap on the
6	machine (RESEARCH Pitfall 1 — discovered live against a real machine during Phase 2
7	research, and only undone with a manual `snap refresh --unhold`). This module never
8	calls it. Hold state is inspected only through the read-only `sudo snap get system
9	refresh.hold` (`validate()`, informational only, never acted on; sudo because snapd
10	admin-gates reading snap config, not because the read changes anything). Convergence uses
11	only `snap install --revision=<N>` and `snap refresh --revision=<N>`, which land the
12	target on the source's exact revision without touching the standing auto-refresh
13	policy at all — the mechanism D-06 requires: both machines converge on the same
14	revision, neither stops updating.
15	
16	The snapd store stays authoritative for its own state (D-01): this job never touches
17	`/var/lib/snapd` directly, only shells out to `snap` itself, the same shape
18	`apt_sync` uses for `apt`/`dpkg`.
19	
20	Snap has no repository or key decision to replicate, and gets no screen for one (D-42).
21	One store serves the device, and name -> publisher is pinned store-side by a
22	canonical-signed `snap-declaration` snapd validates itself, so one name resolves to one
23	snap-id resolves to one publisher and there is no second `firefox` for the target to
24	install by accident. Keys are snapd's own, not the user's. A brand store or a store
25	proxy could in principle make two machines draw from different stores, but both are
26	device-provisioning facts rather than per-snap facts and neither is replicable, so snap
27	is treated as having one store and no store-identity check exists. The provenance
28	variable that remains is which revision of that one snap is installed and which channel
29	it tracks, and D-06 converges both.
30	
31	`SnapSyncJob` subclasses `PackageSyncJob` and implements the abstract `plan()`: what a
32	diff even IS differs per manager, so the base class holds no diff to inherit. apt's own
33	diff lives in `apt_sync` and is apt-package-shaped (a version difference is `REPORT_ONLY`
34	per D-04, with no notion of a tracking channel), while D-06 wants a snap's revision AND
35	channel differences to actively converge (`CHANGE`). `plan()` here reuses the
36	manager-agnostic building blocks the shared core does provide — `DecisionFile`/
37	`filter_inert` (D-08's machine-local skip-always filtering) and
38	`PackageSyncJob._build_review_groups` (D-24's action-grouped review) — so the only
39	genuinely snap-specific code is capture, diff and converge. `accept_review()`, `apply()`
40	and `execute()` are inherited unchanged, and `execute()` is where this job's own single
41	review happens, before its own first mutating command: there is no coordinator and no
42	review spanning two managers (D-15, D-24).
43	
44	Revision AND channel differences share one `DiffAction.CHANGE` diff per snap, tagged
45	`ItemClass.SNAP` in both cases (never `ItemClass.SNAP_CHANNEL`) even though a
46	same-revision retrack is conceptually "just" a channel change: `PackageSyncJob.
47	_build_review_groups` derives one action_label verb per REVIEW GROUP from its first
48	entry's `item_class` (its own docstring flags this as unhandled for "a manager mixing
49	item classes under one action"), so tagging some CHANGE diffs `SNAP` and others
50	`SNAP_CHANNEL` would risk one of the two kinds getting the other's verb whenever both
51	occur in the same run. Using one item_class for every CHANGE diff avoids that
52	mislabeling entirely; the diff's `detail` text still names both revisions or both
53	channels, satisfying D-07's "review names the concrete action" without depending on a
54	shared-core behavior this plan does not own.
55	"""

162	def _parse_snap_list(output: str) -> list[SnapItem]:
163	    """Parse `snap list --all` by HEADER column names, never fixed offsets or assumed
164	    order (RESEARCH Open Question 2): a future snapd column reorder must yield correct
165	    values, never a silently wrong revision driving a wrong `--revision` install.
166	
167	    Skips a disabled older-revision line (`Notes` names `disabled`) for a snap that
168	    also has an active line — only the active revision becomes the item. Output shaped
169	    like "No snaps are installed yet." (no recognizable header) degrades to an empty
170	    list rather than raising: a snap-free machine is a valid, if rare, state.
171	    """
172	    lines = [line for line in output.splitlines() if line.strip()]
173	    if not lines:
174	        return []
175	
176	    header = lines[0].split()
177	    try:
178	        name_idx = header.index("Name")
179	        rev_idx = header.index("Rev")
180	        tracking_idx = header.index("Tracking")
181	        notes_idx = header.index("Notes")
182	    except ValueError:
183	        return []
184	
185	    max_idx = max(name_idx, rev_idx, tracking_idx, notes_idx)
186	    items: list[SnapItem] = []
187	    for line in lines[1:]:
188	        fields = line.split()
189	        if len(fields) <= max_idx:
190	            continue
191	        notes = fields[notes_idx].split(",")
192	        if "disabled" in notes:
193	            continue
194	        # `held` in the Notes column is a PER-SNAP refresh hold (#208, D9) — snapstate
195	        # attached to this one snap. It is SEPARATE state from the system-wide
196	        # `refresh.hold` the orchestrator sets across the sync window via `snap set
197	        # system refresh.hold` (different snapd namespaces), so capturing here, inside
198	        # the sync window, does not mask a per-snap hold: the system hold never writes
199	        # `held` into an individual snap's Notes. If a VM integration test ever shows a
200	        # system hold flipping this token, capture would have to move BEFORE the
201	        # sync-window hold is applied. Fail-safe even then: a system hold flips both
202	        # hosts symmetrically -> both-held -> no spurious diff.
203	        held = "held" in notes
204	        # Confinement, from the same Notes list: snapd refuses to install a classic or a
205	        # devmode revision without the matching flag as explicit confirmation, so the
206	        # capture has to carry it or `_converge_install` cannot build a working command.
207	        items.append(
208	            SnapItem(
209	                name=fields[name_idx],
210	                channel=fields[tracking_idx],
211	                revision=fields[rev_idx],
212	                held=held,
213	                classic="classic" in notes,
214	                devmode="devmode" in notes,
215	            )
216	        )
217	    return items

222	    for this item's confinement, as a leading-space command fragment ("" for a strictly
223	    confined snap).
224	
225	    At most ONE flag is ever emitted, classic winning. The two mean different, mutually
226	    incompatible things — `--classic` confirms a revision the store published with classic
227	    confinement, `--devmode` (per `snap install --help`) "relax[es] confinement for strict
228	    snaps" — so a snap is one or the other, never both. The `snap` CLI only rejects one
229	    mode-flag pair outright (`cannot use devmode and jailmode flags together`, verified in

238	    if item.devmode:
239	        return " --devmode"

329	    intent (a hold on a snap the source no longer has is not the user's current intent).
330	    `sorted` for a stable, deterministic review order.
331	    """
332	    source_by_name = {item.name: item for item in source_items}
333	    target_held = {item.name for item in target_items if item.held}
334	
335	    diffs: list[ItemDiff] = []
336	    for name in sorted(source_by_name):
337	        in_source = source_by_name[name].held
338	        in_target = name in target_held
339	        if in_source == in_target:
340	            continue
341	        diffs.append(_hold_diff(name, in_source=in_source))
342	    return diffs

345	def _diff_snap_items(source_items: Sequence[SnapItem], target_items: Sequence[SnapItem]) -> list[ItemDiff]:
346	    """One diff per snap name present on either side, source-then-target order — same
347	    shape as `PackageSyncJob._diff_apt_packages`, but with D-06's own convergence rule.
348	    Per-snap hold membership diffs follow the presence diffs (D8: install-before-hold).
349	    """
350	    source_by_id = {item.item_id: item for item in source_items}
351	    target_by_id = {item.item_id: item for item in target_items}
352	
353	    seen: dict[str, None] = {}
354	    for item in (*source_items, *target_items):
355	        seen.setdefault(item.item_id, None)
356	
357	    diffs: list[ItemDiff] = []
358	    for item_id in seen:
359	        source_item = source_by_id.get(item_id)
360	        target_item = target_by_id.get(item_id)
361	
362	        if source_item is not None and target_item is None:
363	            diffs.append(_install_diff(source_item))
364	        elif target_item is not None and source_item is None:
365	            diffs.append(_remove_diff(target_item))
366	        elif (
367	            source_item is not None
368	            and target_item is not None
369	            and (source_item.revision != target_item.revision or source_item.channel != target_item.channel)
370	        ):
371	            diffs.append(_change_diff(item_id, source_item, target_item))
372	        # else: present on both, identical revision and channel -> no diff.
373	
374	    # Hold diffs AFTER presence diffs (D8) so a hold on a same-run install lands once the
375	    # snap is present.
376	    diffs.extend(_diff_snap_holds(source_items, target_items))
377	
378	    return diffs

381	def _current_revision_name(app_dir: Path) -> str | None:
382	    """The revision directory name `~/<app>/current` resolves to, or None when the
383	    symlink is missing or dangling.
384	
385	    snapd maintains `current` as a symlink to the active revision's directory. Resolving
386	    it (readlink, followed to the real dir) yields that revision's directory name so the
387	    caller can keep the matching data dir in the mirror (decision 3). A missing or dangling
388	    `current` — the active revision is then indeterminate — returns None, and the caller
389	    falls back to excluding every revision dir for that app (the safe default).
390	    """
391	    current = app_dir / "current"
392	    try:
393	        resolved = current.resolve(strict=True)
394	    except OSError:
395	        return None
396	    if not resolved.is_dir():
397	        return None
398	    return resolved.name
399

401	def snap_sync_exclude_paths() -> list[Path]:
402	    """Absolute `~/snap/<app>/<revision>` data directories folder_sync must NOT mirror,
403	    resolved against `Path.home()` at call time exactly like `vscode_state_exclude_paths()`
404	    — unlike VS Code's fixed relpath list, the revision set is dynamic, so it is enumerated
405	    from the filesystem rather than hardcoded.
406	
407	    Per app this excludes every revision dir EXCEPT the one the app's `current` symlink
408	    resolves to (decision 3, issue #118): snap_sync converges the target onto the source's
409	    revision before folder_sync runs (D-17 order), so by folder_sync time both machines'
410	    `current` points at the same revision, and mirroring THAT revision's data dir carries
411	    the active revision's per-user app data across. The retained older revision dirs stay
412	    excluded so folder_sync never plants data dirs for revisions the target's snapd never
413	    installed.
414	
415	    `~/snap/<app>/common` (revision-independent user data folder_sync must keep mirroring)
416	    and `~/snap/<app>/current` (the symlink itself) are always kept — the whole reason this
417	    export is not simply `~/snap`. When `current` is missing or dangling the active revision
418	    cannot be determined, so ALL of that app's revision dirs are excluded (safe default).
419	    """
420	    snap_root = Path.home() / "snap"
421	    if not snap_root.is_dir():
422	        return []
423	
424	    paths: list[Path] = []
425	    for app_dir in sorted(snap_root.iterdir()):
426	        if not app_dir.is_dir():
427	            continue
428	        current_revision = _current_revision_name(app_dir)
429	        for entry in sorted(app_dir.iterdir()):
430	            if entry.name in _NON_REVISION_DIR_NAMES or not entry.is_dir():
431	                continue
432	            if current_revision is not None and entry.name == current_revision:
433	                continue  # active-revision data dir travels with folder_sync (decision 3)
434	            paths.append(entry)
435	    return paths

438	class SnapSyncJob(PackageSyncJob):
439	    """Converge snap name/channel/revision after the coordinator's batched review.
440	
441	    Overrides `plan()` with a snap-specific capture -> diff -> review-group pipeline
442	    (module docstring explains why the inherited apt-package-shaped one cannot be
443	    reused); `accept_review()`, `apply()` and `execute()` are inherited unchanged.
444	    """
445	
446	    name: ClassVar[str] = "snap_sync"
447	    manager_id: ClassVar[str] = "snap"
448	
449	    # No configurable properties: mirrors AptSyncJob's empty schema — only the enable
450	    # flag in sync_jobs is needed for this slice.
451	    CONFIG_SCHEMA: ClassVar[dict[str, Any]] = {
452	        "type": "object",
453	        "properties": {},
454	        "additionalProperties": False,
455	    }
456	
457	    def __init__(self, context: JobContext) -> None:
458	        super().__init__(context)
459	        # Populated by plan()'s own capture/query step (post filter_inert) and
460	        # consulted by converge(): the base pipeline only ever hands converge() an
461	        # ItemDiff, whose item_id ("snap:<name>") carries no revision/channel data of
462	        # its own — unlike an apt package name, `snap install --revision=N` needs the
463	        # literal N, which has to come from somewhere other than the diff itself.
464	        self._source_items_by_id: dict[str, SnapItem] = {}
465	        self._target_items_by_id: dict[str, SnapItem] = {}
466	
467	    async def capture_source_items(self) -> Sequence[SnapItem]:  # pyright: ignore[reportIncompatibleMethodOverride]
468	        """`snap list --all` on the source (D-06).
469	
470	        This job overrides `plan()` and never routes through `PackageSyncJob.
471	        diff_items`'s apt-package-shaped dispatch (module docstring), so widening this
472	        hook's item type here is safe: no code holding a `PackageSyncJob`-typed
473	        reference ever calls it expecting an `AptPackageItem` back.
474	
475	        Guarded on the exit code (ADR-022). This is the read whose silence is worst: an
476	        empty source manifest offers every snap on the target for removal, and the only
477	        thing standing between that and a wiped target is that removal groups arrive
478	        unticked. Measured against the real `snap` binary — with snapd unreachable it exits
479	        1, and with snapd answering that zero snaps are installed it exits 0, writes "No
480	        snaps are installed yet." to STDERR and leaves stdout empty. So the exit code
481	        separates the two cleanly, and an empty stdout at exit 0 is a machine with no snaps,
482	        which is an ordinary machine.
483	        """
484	        command = "snap list --all"
485	        result = await self.source.run_command(command)
486	        require_answer(command, result, Host.SOURCE)
487	        return _parse_snap_list(result.stdout)
488	
489	    async def query_target_items(self) -> Sequence[SnapItem]:  # pyright: ignore[reportIncompatibleMethodOverride]
490	        """The target's own `snap list --all` (same reasoning as `capture_source_items`)."""
491	        command = "snap list --all"
492	        result = await self.target.run_command(command, login_shell=False)
493	        require_answer(command, result, Host.TARGET)
494	        return _parse_snap_list(result.stdout)
495	
496	    @override
497	    async def plan(self) -> PackagePlan:
498	        """Load decision files -> capture -> query -> diff -> build review groups.
499	
500	        Read-only: only `snap list --all` (both machines) and a decision-file `cat`
501	        run here — no `snap install`/`refresh`/`switch`/`remove` before this returns.
502	        Caches the filtered source/target items by id for `converge()` (see
503	        `__init__`), since `ItemDiff.item_id` alone carries no revision/channel data.
504	
505	        Sideloaded source snaps are reported once and dropped from the diff input:
506	        reproducing them is not implemented (there is no mechanism to carry the `.snap`
507	        bytes to the target), so every diff they could produce — install, revision/channel
508	        change, and the `snap:hold:` diff `_diff_snap_holds` derives from a source snap —
509	        would be an item that can only fail at converge, every run. A warning states that
510	        once; no review item is emitted, since the user has no action to take on it.
511	        """
512	        source_decisions = await DecisionFile(self.manager_id, self.source).load()
513	        target_decisions = await DecisionFile(self.manager_id, self.target).load()
514	
515	        source_items = await filter_inert(await self.capture_source_items(), source_decisions)
516	        target_items = await filter_inert(await self.query_target_items(), target_decisions)
517	
518	        source_items, sideloaded = _partition_sideloaded(source_items)
519	        if sideloaded:
520	            self._log(
521	                Host.SOURCE,
522	                LogLevel.WARNING,
523	                "Skipping snap(s) installed from a local file: their revision exists in no store, so they "
524	                "cannot be reproduced on the target — "
525	                + ", ".join(f"{item.name} (revision {item.revision})" for item in sideloaded),
526	            )
527	            # The target's own entry for those names goes with them. Dropping only the
528	            # source side would leave the target's copy unmatched, and an unmatched target
529	            # snap is an EXTRA_ON_TARGET removal — turning "cannot reproduce this" into
530	            # "propose deleting it there". A sideloaded snap the source does NOT have stays
531	            # an ordinary removal candidate: its name is not in this set.
532	            withheld = {item.name for item in sideloaded}
533	            target_items = [item for item in target_items if item.name not in withheld]
534	
535	        self._source_items_by_id = {item.item_id: item for item in source_items}
536	        self._target_items_by_id = {item.item_id: item for item in target_items}
537	
538	        # `_drop_inert_diffs` after the diff, not `filter_inert` before it: a hold's
539	        # identity is `snap:hold:<name>`, which no `SnapItem` carries (its own id is
540	        # `snap:<name>`), so a recorded hold decision can only be matched on the ItemDiff.
541	        diffs = self._drop_inert_diffs(
542	            _diff_snap_items(source_items, target_items), source_decisions, target_decisions
543	        )
544	        groups = self._build_review_groups(diffs)
545	        return PackagePlan(manager=self.manager_id, diffs=diffs, groups=groups)
546	
547	    @override
548	    async def converge(self, diff: ItemDiff) -> CommandResult:
549	        """Install/refresh at the source's explicit revision, switch channel only when
550	        it differs, or remove (never purge) — the only D-06-safe verbs (module
551	        docstring). One snap per invocation (D-27) so a single bad snap cannot fail the
552	        whole batch.
553	
554	        Hold membership items (`snap:hold:<name>`) are routed FIRST, by item_id prefix
555	        (#208, D4), so a `snap:hold:` INSTALL runs `snap refresh --hold=forever` rather
556	        than a snap install, and a `snap:hold:` REMOVE (unhold) is never misread as a
557	        snap removal. This test MUST precede the action-based dispatch below, because
558	        `snap:hold:` also matches the plain `snap:` prefix.
559	        """
560	        if diff.item_id.startswith(_SNAP_HOLD_ID_PREFIX):
561	            return await self._converge_hold(diff)
562	
563	        if diff.action == DiffAction.REMOVE:
564	            return await self._converge_remove(diff)
565	
566	        source_item = self._source_items_by_id.get(diff.item_id)
567	        if source_item is None:
568	            raise ConvergeItemFailed(
569	                f"no captured source snap for {diff.label} (item_id={diff.item_id!r}); "
570	                "was plan() run before converge()?"
571	            )
572	
573	        if diff.action == DiffAction.INSTALL:
574	            return await self._converge_install(source_item)
575	        if diff.action == DiffAction.CHANGE:
576	            target_item = self._target_items_by_id.get(diff.item_id)
577	            return await self._converge_change(source_item, target_item)
578	
579	        raise ConvergeItemFailed(f"SnapSyncJob.converge: unsupported action {diff.action.value!r} for {diff.label}")
580	
581	    async def _converge_install(self, source_item: SnapItem) -> CommandResult:
582	        """`snap install --revision=<N>` lands the exact revision without ever
583	        touching a hold (D-06); the channel switch always follows so the target
584	        tracks the same channel as the source. There is no cheap way to learn
585	        "snapd's default channel for a not-yet-installed snap" from `snap list --all`
586	        alone (only installed snaps appear in it), and re-running `switch` to a
587	        channel the install already landed on is a harmless no-op, so always
588	        switching is simpler and no less correct than conditioning on that unknown.
589	
590	        The SOURCE item's confinement flag is interpolated because snapd requires it as
591	        explicit per-revision confirmation: without `--classic`, installing a
592	        classic-confinement snap fails with "repeat the command including --classic" on
593	        every run, forever. `--revision=N` does NOT bypass that check — snapd's own
594	        wording is "This revision of snap %q was published using classic confinement".
595	        """
596	        name = shlex.quote(source_item.name)
597	        revision = shlex.quote(source_item.revision)
598	        install_result = await self.target.run_command(
599	            f"sudo snap install{_confinement_flags(source_item)} --revision={revision} {name}",
600	            login_shell=False,
601	            mutates=f"install snap {source_item.name} at revision {source_item.revision}",
602	        )
603	        if not install_result.success:
604	            return install_result
605	        return await self._switch_channel(source_item)
606	
607	    async def _converge_change(self, source_item: SnapItem, target_item: SnapItem | None) -> CommandResult:
608	        """`snap refresh --revision=<N>` when the revision differs, plus the channel
609	        switch when the channel also differs (or is the only thing that differs) —
610	        `converge()` only reaches here for a diff `_diff_snap_items` built because at
611	        least one of the two was true.
612	
613	        The refresh carries the SOURCE item's confinement flag for the same reason the
614	        install does. `snap refresh --help` says a plain refresh preserves the snap's
615	        existing confinement options, but that describes the TARGET's current confinement,
616	        which is the wrong one whenever the two hosts disagree: source classic + target
617	        strict is a real case (a snap that changed confinement between the two installed
618	        revisions), and refreshing onto the source's classic revision without `--classic`
619	        hits the same per-revision refusal an install would. The flag is therefore always
620	        passed rather than conditioned on the target — the safe direction, since `--classic`
621	        on a snap that does not need it is only a warning ("flag --classic ignored for
622	        strictly confined snap"), whereas omitting it where it IS needed is a hard failure
623	        on every run.
624	
625	        The reverse skew (source strict, target classic) emits no flag and leaves the
626	        target's confinement as-is: confinement is not part of item identity and never
627	        produces a diff of its own, so there is nothing here proposing to converge it.
628	        """
629	        revision_differs = target_item is None or source_item.revision != target_item.revision
630	        channel_differs = target_item is None or source_item.channel != target_item.channel
631	
632	        result: CommandResult | None = None
633	        if revision_differs:
634	            name = shlex.quote(source_item.name)
635	            revision = shlex.quote(source_item.revision)
636	            result = await self.target.run_command(
637	                f"sudo snap refresh{_confinement_flags(source_item)} --revision={revision} {name}",
638	                login_shell=False,
639	                mutates=f"move snap {source_item.name} to revision {source_item.revision}",
640	            )
641	            if not result.success:
642	                return result
643	
644	        if channel_differs:
645	            result = await self._switch_channel(source_item)
646	
647	        assert result is not None, "converge() only calls this for a diff where something differed at plan time"
648	        return result
649	
650	    async def _switch_channel(self, source_item: SnapItem) -> CommandResult:
651	        name = shlex.quote(source_item.name)
652	        channel = shlex.quote(source_item.channel)
653	        return await self.target.run_command(
654	            f"sudo snap switch --channel={channel} {name}",
655	            login_shell=False,
656	            mutates=f"track channel {source_item.channel} for snap {source_item.name}",
657	        )
658	
659	    async def _converge_remove(self, diff: ItemDiff) -> CommandResult:
660	        """`snap remove`, never `--purge`: purge discards snapd's own pre-removal
661	        snapshot, which is the user's only recovery path if the removal was a mistake.
662	        """
663	        name = shlex.quote(_snap_name(diff.item_id))
664	        return await self.target.run_command(
665	            f"sudo snap remove {name}",
666	            login_shell=False,
667	            mutates=f"remove snap {_snap_name(diff.item_id)}",
668	        )
669	
670	    async def _converge_hold(self, diff: ItemDiff) -> CommandResult:
671	        """Converge one `snap:hold:<name>` membership item (#208, D4/D6): INSTALL ->
672	        `snap refresh --hold=forever <name>` (per-snap hold on the target), REMOVE ->
673	        `snap refresh --unhold <name>`.
674	
675	        CRITICAL (module docstring, RESEARCH Pitfall 1): the snap name is ALWAYS
676	        interpolated, so this never degenerates into a bare `snap refresh --hold` — the
677	        form that silently sets an INDEFINITE GLOBAL hold on every snap. The name comes
678	        from the item_id's `snap:hold:` suffix, which `_diff_snap_holds` only ever built
679	        from a concrete source/target snap name, so it is never empty.
680	
681	        Selection state only, no gating (D6): a hold on a snap the user skipped
682	        installing this run hits an absent snap and fails — that is a normal per-item
683	        failure (D-27, the exit code alone decides pass/fail), not a gated abort.
684	        """
685	        raw_name = diff.item_id.removeprefix(_SNAP_HOLD_ID_PREFIX)
686	        name = shlex.quote(raw_name)
687	        flag = "--hold=forever" if diff.action == DiffAction.INSTALL else "--unhold"
688	        verb = "hold" if diff.action == DiffAction.INSTALL else "unhold"
689	        return await self.target.run_command(
690	            f"sudo snap refresh {flag} {name}",
691	            login_shell=False,
692	            mutates=f"{verb} snap {raw_name}",
693	        )

695	    @override
696	    async def validate(self) -> list[ValidationError]:
697	        """`snap version` on both ends, passwordless `sudo --non-interactive true` on BOTH ends, and a
698	        read-only informational hold check on both ends (never acted on — module docstring).
699	        Sequential checks appending to `errors`, matching `AptSyncJob.validate()`'s shape.
700	
701	        Passwordless sudo is now required on the SOURCE too, not just the target: the
702	        orchestrator pauses snapd auto-refresh across the sync window by writing
703	        `refresh.hold` via `sudo snap set system` on both hosts (decision 4), so the source
704	        needs the same `sudo --non-interactive` grant for `/usr/bin/snap` that the target already needed
705	        for install/refresh/remove.
706	        """
707	        errors: list[ValidationError] = []
708	
709	        source_check = await self.source.run_command("snap version")
710	        if not source_check.success:
711	            errors.append(self._validation_error(Host.SOURCE, "snap is not available on source"))
712	
713	        target_check = await self.target.run_command("snap version", login_shell=False)
714	        if not target_check.success:
715	            errors.append(self._validation_error(Host.TARGET, "snap is not available on target"))
716	
717	        source_sudo_check = await self.source.run_command("sudo --non-interactive true")
718	        if not source_sudo_check.success:
719	            errors.append(
720	                self._validation_error(
721	                    Host.SOURCE,
722	                    "passwordless sudo is not available on source "
723	                    "(required to pause snapd auto-refresh for the sync window).\n"
724	                    + passwordless_sudo_hint(_TARGET_SUDO_COMMANDS),
725	                )
726	            )
727	
728	        sudo_check = await self.target.run_command("sudo --non-interactive true", login_shell=False)
729	        if not sudo_check.success:
730	            errors.append(
731	                self._validation_error(
732	                    Host.TARGET,
733	                    "passwordless sudo is not available on target "
734	                    "(required for snap install/refresh/remove).\n"
735	                    + passwordless_sudo_hint(_TARGET_SUDO_COMMANDS, user=self.context.target_username),
736	                )
737	            )
738	
739	        # Read-only informational context (RESEARCH Pitfall 1): NEVER `snap refresh
740	        # --hold` with no arguments to check this — that form mutates. A pre-existing
741	        # hold is not itself an error here; it only explains why a revision might not
742	        # converge, so it is logged, never appended to `errors`.
743	        # Under sudo: snapd admin-gates READING snap config (`io.snapcraft.snapd.manage-
744	        # configuration`, `auth_admin_keep`), so unprivileged this does not report "no hold",
745	        # it fails with "access denied" and the line below would say `(none)` unconditionally.
746	        source_hold = await self.source.run_command("sudo snap get system refresh.hold")
747	        self._log(Host.SOURCE, LogLevel.FULL, f"source snap refresh.hold: {source_hold.stdout.strip() or '(none)'}")
748	        target_hold = await self.target.run_command("sudo snap get system refresh.hold", login_shell=False)
749	        self._log(Host.TARGET, LogLevel.FULL, f"target snap refresh.hold: {target_hold.stdout.strip() or '(none)'}")
750	
751	        return errors

1	"""`manual_installs_sync`: the fourth package job, owning everything no package manager
2	can reproduce (D-15, D-18, D-19, D-20, D-21).
3	
4	Two detectors, both run on the SOURCE:
5	
6	- apt packages in the source's `apt-mark showmanual` set whose INSTALLED version comes
7	  from no repository the source has configured — installed via `dpkg --install` of a bare
8	  `.deb`, so only dpkg's own status file accounts for them.
9	- paths directly under `/usr/local` and `/opt` (plus the immediate children of
10	  `/usr/local/bin` and `/usr/local/lib`) that no dpkg package owns — software an install
11	  script dropped there, bypassing apt entirely.
12	
13	D-18 gives them their own job and their own enable flag, because half of what they cover is
14	not apt's business at all (unowned files under `/usr/local`/`/opt`), and folding them into
15	`apt_sync` would make disabling apt silently disable manual-install detection with nothing
16	telling the user. This job does its OWN `dpkg`/`apt-cache` queries rather than sharing
17	`apt_sync`'s, so ownership stays clean — it never imports `apt_sync` (D-18). The
18	`apt-cache policy` PARSING both jobs need lives in `packages/apt_policy.py`, a third
19	module neither job owns.
20	
21	An unreproducible item ends an interactive run resolved in one of three ways (D-21,
22	decision 10): it has an install snippet in the shared, synced registry (`SnippetRegistry`,
23	D-20/D-23), it is recorded machine-specific (skip-always) in this job's machine-local
24	decision file, or the user skipped it once — skip-once is a real decision. There is no
25	fourth "genuinely undecided" outcome an interactive review can reach: an empty snippet
26	capture re-prompts rather than falling through, and Ctrl-C/EOF aborts the whole sync
27	(`SyncAbortedByUser`) instead of leaving an item unresolved.
28	
29	`ManualInstallsSyncJob` subclasses `PackageSyncJob` and overrides `plan()`, `converge()`,

86	# D-19's bounded unowned-install scan: top-level entries of `/usr/local` and `/opt`, plus
87	# the immediate children of `/usr/local/bin` and `/usr/local/lib` — one batched
88	# `find <dir...> -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1` covers all four, since `find` applies the same
89	# depth options to every starting path it is given. Enough to NAME a finding (D-18), never
90	# enough to walk an entire tree — the item is decided on, not replicated (deferred ideas,
91	# CONTEXT.md). Owned by this job now, no longer shared with apt_sync (D-18).
92	_UNOWNED_SCAN_ROOTS = ("/usr/local", "/opt", "/usr/local/bin", "/usr/local/lib")
93	
94	# Matches one `dpkg --search` "owned" line: `<package>[,<package>...]: <path>`. A path dpkg does
95	# not own produces no such line at all (its "no path found" diagnostic goes to stderr,
96	# which this scan never inspects) — absence from stdout is the only signal
97	# `_owned_paths_from_dpkg_s` needs. A private copy of apt_sync's identical regex: D-18
98	# keeps ownership clean by NOT importing apt_sync, and this parser is small enough that
99	# one duplicated line is cheaper than a shared-core coupling.
100	_DPKG_S_OWNED_RE = re.compile(r"^[^:]+:\s+(?P<path>/\S.*)$")

108	@dataclass(frozen=True)
109	class UnreproducibleItem:
110	    """One item no package manager can reproduce (D-18): an apt package installed from no
111	    configured repository, or an unowned install under `/usr/local`/`/opt`.
112	
113	    `origin` distinguishes how the item was found — `apt-no-candidate` (an installed
114	    package no repository can supply) versus `unowned-path` (a filesystem path dpkg does
115	    not claim) — and lives inside `item_id` for the same reason `scope`
116	    lives inside the two flatpak identities: the same `identifier` value can appear
117	    under both origins with no relation to each other (e.g. a package name that is
118	    also, coincidentally, a path component), so origin has to be part of identity, not
119	    just a field alongside it.
120	
121	    Unlike the other item types, `label` here is a plain FIELD rather than a `label()`
122	    method: the human-readable description comes from whichever detector found the
123	    item (D-19's unowned-install scan, or the no-candidate check) and is not something
124	    this dataclass can derive from `origin`/`identifier` alone.
125	    """
126	
127	    origin: Literal["apt-no-candidate", "unowned-path"]
128	    identifier: str
129	    label: str
130	
131	    ITEM_CLASS: ClassVar[ItemClass] = ItemClass.UNREPRODUCIBLE
132	
133	    @property
134	    def item_id(self) -> str:
135	        """Stable identity string: `unreproducible:<origin>:<identifier>`."""
136	        return f"unreproducible:{self.origin}:{self.identifier}"
137	
138	
139	def _lines(output: str) -> list[str]:
140	    """Non-blank, stripped lines — the shape every `apt-mark`/`find` list command this
141	    module runs produces. A private copy of apt_sync's identical helper (D-18)."""
142	    return [line.strip() for line in output.splitlines() if line.strip()]
143	
144	
145	def _owned_paths_from_dpkg_s(output: str) -> frozenset[str]:
146	    """Every path `dpkg --search` reports as owned, parsed from its stdout alone (D-19's
147	    unowned-install scan). A queried path dpkg does NOT own is simply absent from this set
148	    — its "no path found matching pattern" diagnostic is a stderr message this scan never
149	    reads, so a batched multi-path `dpkg --search` degrades cleanly even when some paths are
150	    unowned and others are not. A private copy of apt_sync's identical parser (D-18).
151	    """
152	    owned: set[str] = set()
153	    for line in output.splitlines():
154	        match = _DPKG_S_OWNED_RE.match(line)
155	        if match:
156	            owned.add(match.group("path"))
157	    return frozenset(owned)

163	
164	    Overrides `plan()` with an unreproducible-specific detect -> filter -> diff pipeline
165	    (the inherited apt-package-shaped `diff_items` does not apply); `converge()` replays a
166	    registered install snippet verbatim (D-20); the unreproducible finalize hook the base
167	    leaves as a no-op is implemented here.
168	    """
169	
170	    name: ClassVar[str] = "manual_installs_sync"
171	    manager_id: ClassVar[str] = "manual"
172	
173	    # No configurable properties: mirrors AptSyncJob's empty schema — only the enable flag
174	    # in sync_jobs is needed. D-32 forbids an empty placeholder config SECTION, so there is
175	    # no `manual_installs_sync:` block in default-config.yaml, but the in-code CONFIG_SCHEMA
176	    # ClassVar still declares the empty object every job carries.
177	    CONFIG_SCHEMA: ClassVar[dict[str, Any]] = {
178	        "type": "object",
179	        "properties": {},
180	        "additionalProperties": False,
181	    }

183	    def __init__(self, context: JobContext) -> None:
184	        super().__init__(context)
185	        # Guards `_finalize_unreproducible` to run at most once per run. `after_review()`
186	        # calls it (so the pushed registry includes on-the-fly snippets), then the base
187	        # `apply()` calls it again; the second call is a no-op so a snippet's `authored_at`
188	        # is stamped exactly once and the source and pushed target registries stay identical.
189	        self._unreproducible_finalized = False
190	
191	    # -- after-review snippet push (D-23) -----------------------------------------------
192	
193	    @override
194	    async def after_review(self) -> None:
195	        """Push the install-snippet registry to the target after this job's review and
196	        before `apply()` replays any snippet (D-23), then promote each on-the-fly-authored
197	        item so it is APPLIED — not merely transported — the same run.
198	
199	        Finalize-then-push-then-promote: `_finalize_unreproducible` persists this run's
200	        authored snippets into the SOURCE registry first (idempotent — `apply()` calls it
201	        again as a no-op), then `_push_snippet_registry` copies that file to the target,
202	        and finally `_promote_authored_snippets_to_install` reclassifies each authored
203	        item's diff `REPORT_ONLY -> INSTALL` decided `APPLY` so the unchanged base
204	        `apply()` converges it this run rather than the next one. Promotion runs AFTER the
205	        push so the target already holds the snippet the replay reads. The push depends on
206	        no other job: it moves the file itself and reads neither `config_sync` nor
207	        `folder_sync` state, so disabling either cannot break snippet delivery.
208	        """
209	        assert self._accepted_plan is not None
210	        assert self._accepted_outcome is not None
211	        await self._finalize_unreproducible(self._accepted_plan, self._accepted_outcome)
212	        await self._push_snippet_registry()
213	        self._promote_authored_snippets_to_install()
214	
215	    def _promote_authored_snippets_to_install(self) -> None:
216	        """Reclassify every on-the-fly-authored item's diff `REPORT_ONLY -> INSTALL` and
217	        force its decision to `APPLY`, so the unchanged base `apply()` — which converges
218	        only APPLY-decided, non-`REPORT_ONLY` diffs (`sync_core.py` apply_diffs filter) —
219	        replays the freshly authored snippet THIS run, closing the one-run-too-late gap.
220	
221	        Called from `after_review()` only after the authored snippets are persisted to the
222	        source registry and pushed to the target, so the target holds the snippet by the
223	        time the promoted diff converges. The add-snippet review path records no decision
224	        for the item (`packages.review._review_unreproducible_group`), so the decision must
225	        be forced here in addition to reclassifying the action.
226	
227	        Mutates only in-memory accepted state (a `dataclasses.replace` of the frozen plan
228	        and outcome), so it is safe under dry-run: `apply()`'s dry-run branch previews a
229	        would-install line and issues no converge, preserving ADR-014.
230	        """
231	        assert self._accepted_plan is not None
232	        assert self._accepted_outcome is not None
233	        outcome = self._accepted_outcome
234	        if not outcome.snippets:
235	            return
236	
237	        plan = self._accepted_plan
238	        authored = frozenset(outcome.snippets)
239	        new_diffs = tuple(
240	            replace(diff, action=DiffAction.INSTALL)
241	            if diff.item_id in authored and diff.action is DiffAction.REPORT_ONLY
242	            else diff
243	            for diff in plan.diffs
244	        )
245	        new_decisions = dict(outcome.decisions)
246	        for item_id in authored:
247	            new_decisions[item_id] = Decision.APPLY
248	
249	        self._accepted_plan = replace(plan, diffs=new_diffs)
250	        self._accepted_outcome = replace(outcome, decisions=new_decisions)

252	    async def _push_snippet_registry(self) -> None:
253	        """Copy the source's `~/.config/pc-switcher/package-snippets.yaml` to the target's
254	        own copy under the SSH user's home, mirroring `config_sync._copy_config_to_target`'s
255	        `mkdir --parents` -> `echo $HOME` -> `send_file` shape.
256	
257	        `send_file` writes plain SFTP as the SSH user, always under that user's home
258	        (`~/.config/pc-switcher`) — never `/etc` — which is exactly where the registry
259	        belongs, so no `sudo install` staging is needed. A no-op if the source has no
260	        registry file yet (a user who has never authored a snippet) and under dry-run
261	        (ADR-014: a rehearsal transfers nothing).
262	
263	        The push is a WHOLE-FILE overwrite (no per-entry merge). Before it runs,
264	        `_guard_registry_overwrite` compares the target's current registry against the
265	        source's on-disk file (decision 9): a purely additive push (source superset of
266	        target) proceeds silently, while one that would lose or change a target entry
267	        requires explicit confirmation and otherwise aborts the run.
268	        """
269	        if self.context.dry_run:
270	            return
271	
272	        source_path = Path.home() / SNIPPET_REGISTRY_RELPATH
273	        if not source_path.exists():
274	            return
275	
276	        await self._guard_registry_overwrite(source_path)
277	
278	        mkdir = await self.target.run_command(
279	            f"mkdir --parents {CONFIG_REMOTE_DIR}", mutates="create the pc-switcher config directory on the target"
280	        )
281	        if not mkdir.success:
282	            raise RuntimeError(f"Failed to create config directory on target: {mkdir.stderr}")
283	
284	        # send_file needs an absolute remote path, so expand the target's ~ once.
285	        home = await self.target.run_command("echo $HOME")
286	        if not home.success:
287	            raise RuntimeError("Failed to get home directory on target")
288	        absolute_remote_path = f"{home.stdout.strip()}/{SNIPPET_REGISTRY_RELPATH}"
289	        await self.target.send_file(
290	            source_path, absolute_remote_path, mutates="push the install-snippet registry to the target"
291	        )
292	
293	    async def _guard_registry_overwrite(self, source_path: Path) -> None:
294	        """Gate the wholesale `package-snippets.yaml` overwrite on the loss/change of any
295	        target entry (decision 9).
296	
297	        The source's on-disk file (the exact bytes about to be sent) is compared against
298	        the target's current registry per `item_id`. The push is purely additive when the
299	        source is a superset of the target — every target entry is present in the source
300	        with an identical body — in which case it proceeds silently, as before. Otherwise
301	        the target holds an entry that a wholesale overwrite would LOSE (absent from the
302	        source) or CHANGE (a differing body); the user is shown exactly which entries and
303	        must confirm. Declining, or a non-interactive run that cannot confirm, aborts the
304	        whole sync (`SyncAbortedByUser`) so the user can consolidate the two registries by
305	        hand and re-run — the tool never silently discards a snippet only the target has.
306	        """
307	        source_snippets = load_snippets_from_text(source_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
308	        target_snippets = await SnippetRegistry(self.target).load()
309	
310	        lost = [snippet for item_id, snippet in target_snippets.items() if item_id not in source_snippets]
311	        changed = [
312	            (snippet, source_snippets[item_id])
313	            for item_id, snippet in target_snippets.items()
314	            if item_id in source_snippets and source_snippets[item_id].body != snippet.body
315	        ]
316	        if not lost and not changed:
317	            return  # purely additive — source is a superset of the target
318	
319	        assert self.context.confirmer is not None, (
320	            "a non-additive snippet registry overwrite needs a confirmer to gate it"
321	        )
322	        approved = await self.context.confirmer.confirm(
323	            title="Snippet registry overwrite is not purely additive",
324	            message=self._render_overwrite_diff(lost, changed),
325	            # No override flag exists: a lossy overwrite is only ever approved by a human
326	            # answering the prompt, so `allow=False` makes any non-interactive run refuse
327	            # (and thus abort) rather than silently overwrite.
328	            allow=False,
329	            allow_flag="manual registry consolidation",
330	            log_extra={"job": self.name, "host": "source"},
331	        )
332	        if not approved:
333	            raise SyncAbortedByUser(
334	                "snippet registry overwrite declined: the target holds snippet entries "
335	                "absent from or differing in the source that a wholesale push would lose "
336	                "or change; consolidate the two registries by hand and re-run"
337	            )
338	
339	    @staticmethod
340	    def _render_overwrite_diff(lost: list[Snippet], changed: list[tuple[Snippet, Snippet]]) -> str:
341	        """Rich-markup body naming every target entry a wholesale push would lose or change.
342	
343	        Every snippet field is untrusted package-manager/user text, so each is
344	        `rich.markup.escape`d before it reaches the confirmer's `Panel` — a body or label
345	        containing `[...]` must not be parsed as console markup (T-02-02).
346	        """
347	
348	        def body_lines(body: str, indent: str) -> list[str]:
349	            return [f"{indent}{escape(line)}" for line in (body.splitlines() or [""])]
350	
351	        lines = ["The target's snippet registry holds entries this overwrite would discard or replace:", ""]
352	        for snippet in lost:
353	            lines.append(f"  LOST     {escape(snippet.label)}  ({escape(snippet.item_id)})")
354	            lines.extend(body_lines(snippet.body, "             "))
355	        for target_snippet, source_snippet in changed:
356	            lines.append(f"  CHANGED  {escape(target_snippet.label)}  ({escape(target_snippet.item_id)})")
357	            lines.append("             target (to be replaced):")
358	            lines.extend(body_lines(target_snippet.body, "               "))
359	            lines.append("             source (incoming):")
360	            lines.extend(body_lines(source_snippet.body, "               "))
361	        lines += [
362	            "",
363	            "Continuing overwrites the target's registry wholesale. Decline to abort and "
364	            "consolidate the two registries by hand.",
365	        ]
366	        return "\n".join(lines)

368	    # -- Detection (D-18/D-19), all on the source ---------------------------------------
369	
370	    async def _scan_no_candidate_apt_packages(self, manual_names: Sequence[str]) -> list[UnreproducibleItem]:
371	        """D-18: manually-installed packages whose INSTALLED version comes from no
372	        repository the SOURCE has configured — put there by `dpkg --install` of a bare `.deb`.
373	
374	        One batched `apt-cache policy` over the whole manual set (never one call per
375	        package), read through `packages_installed_from_no_repository`: a package's own
376	        `Candidate:` line cannot answer this, because dpkg's status entry makes apt report
377	        a hand-installed package's installed version as its candidate.
378	
379	        Guarded on the exit code AND on the block count (ADR-022 D-04), which is the guard
380	        `apt_sync._source_policy` puts on the byte-identical command: same names, same host,
381	        same probe, so the same strictness. Its silence indicts nothing on its own — an
382	        unanswered probe reports no unreproducible packages, which proposes nothing — but
383	        it does not stay harmless in a whole run: `apt_sync.capture_source_items` DROPS the
384	        same bare-`.deb` packages from its own manifest off its own copy of this probe, so
385	        one probe answering and the other not makes a package vanish from the run with
386	        nothing said about it anywhere. Every name here came from this machine's own
387	        `apt-mark showmanual`, so apt owes a block for each and no block at all is apt not
388	        answering rather than a machine with unusual packages.
389	        """
390	        if not manual_names:
391	            return []
392	
393	        quoted = " ".join(shlex.quote(name) for name in manual_names)
394	        command = f"apt-cache policy {quoted}"
395	        result = await self.source.run_command(command)
396	        # A key per block apt printed, whatever it said inside it — so this counts blocks and
397	        # not packages, and a machine whose whole manual set is bare `.deb`s still answers.
398	        require_answer(
399	            command,
400	            result,
401	            Host.SOURCE,
402	            answers=len(installed_origins_by_package(result.stdout)),
403	            answer_noun="package block",
404	        )
405	        no_repository = packages_installed_from_no_repository(result.stdout, manual_names)
406	        return [
407	            UnreproducibleItem(
408	                origin="apt-no-candidate",
409	                identifier=name,
410	                label=f"{name} (installed from no configured repository)",
411	            )
412	            for name in sorted(no_repository)
413	        ]
414	
415	    async def _scan_unowned_installs(self) -> list[UnreproducibleItem]:
416	        """D-18/D-19: paths under `/usr/local` and `/opt` that no dpkg package owns —
417	        software an install script dropped there directly, bypassing apt entirely.
418	
419	        One batched `find` over `_UNOWNED_SCAN_ROOTS` names every candidate path, then one
420	        batched `dpkg --search` over those candidates decides ownership; a path absent from the
421	        `dpkg --search` output is unowned. Both steps run on the SOURCE (D-18) — a fact about
422	        what the source machine has installed, not the target.
423	
424	        Neither step is guarded, and both are ADR-022 counter-examples rather than
425	        omissions. `dpkg --search` exits 1 as soon as ONE queried path is unowned, which is
426	        precisely the finding this scan is looking for, so a non-zero exit here carries no
427	        information about whether dpkg answered. The `find` already discards its own stderr
428	        and tolerates an absent scan root by design.
429	        """
430	        quoted_roots = " ".join(shlex.quote(root) for root in _UNOWNED_SCAN_ROOTS)
431	        listing = await self.source.run_command(f"find {quoted_roots} -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 2>/dev/null")
432	        candidates = _lines(listing.stdout)
433	        if not candidates:
434	            return []
435	
436	        quoted_paths = " ".join(shlex.quote(path) for path in candidates)
437	        ownership = await self.source.run_command(f"dpkg --search {quoted_paths}")
438	        owned = _owned_paths_from_dpkg_s(ownership.stdout)
439	
440	        return [
441	            UnreproducibleItem(origin="unowned-path", identifier=path, label=path)
442	            for path in sorted(set(candidates) - owned)
443	        ]
444	
445	    # -- plan() / converge() ------------------------------------------------------------
446	
447	    async def capture_source_items(self) -> Sequence[UnreproducibleItem]:  # pyright: ignore[reportIncompatibleMethodOverride]
448	        """The source's unreproducible items: apt-no-candidate packages plus unowned
449	        `/usr/local`/`/opt` installs (D-18). `apt-mark showmanual` runs once here and its
450	        result feeds the no-candidate scan.
451	
452	        This job overrides `plan()` and never routes through `PackageSyncJob.diff_items`'s
453	        apt-package-shaped dispatch, so widening this hook's item type is safe (same
454	        reasoning as `SnapSyncJob.capture_source_items`).
455	        """
456	        command = "apt-mark showmanual"
457	        manual = await self.source.run_command(command)
458	        require_answer(command, manual, Host.SOURCE)
459	        manual_names = _lines(manual.stdout)
460	        return [
461	            *await self._scan_no_candidate_apt_packages(manual_names),
462	            *await self._scan_unowned_installs(),
463	        ]
464	
465	    async def query_target_items(self) -> Sequence[UnreproducibleItem]:  # pyright: ignore[reportIncompatibleMethodOverride]
466	        """No target-side manifest exists for unreproducible items: they are always
467	        source-held (they describe what the SOURCE machine has installed), and convergence
468	        is driven by the shared snippet registry, not by a diff against target state. The
469	        empty result keeps the abstract hook satisfied without a meaningless target query.
470	        """
471	        return []
472	
473	    @override
474	    async def plan(self) -> PackagePlan:
475	        """Detect -> filter inert -> diff against the SOURCE's snippet registry. Read-only.
476	
477	        An item already recorded machine-specific on the SOURCE is dropped by
478	        `filter_inert` before it becomes a diff (D-08/D-19: a finding produces noise
479	        exactly once, then never again). Unreproducible items are always source-held, so
480	        only the source's decision file is consulted.
481	
482	        Reproducibility is judged from the SOURCE — the machine being replicated (corrected
483	        D-23): an item with a source-side registry snippet plans `INSTALL` (a snippet makes
484	        it reproducible), one without plans `REPORT_ONLY` and surfaces in its own review
485	        group for resolution. `after_review()`'s `send_file()` push places that snippet on
486	        the target before `converge()` reads it, so convergence still replays from the
487	        target's copy — only the classification authority moved to the source.
488	        """
489	        source_decisions = await DecisionFile(self.manager_id, self.source).load()
490	        items = await filter_inert(await self.capture_source_items(), source_decisions)
491	
492	        registry = SnippetRegistry(self.source)
493	        diffs: list[ItemDiff] = []
494	        for item in items:
495	            snippet = await registry.get(item.item_id)
496	            action = DiffAction.INSTALL if snippet is not None else DiffAction.REPORT_ONLY
497	            diffs.append(
498	                ItemDiff(
499	                    item_class=ItemClass.UNREPRODUCIBLE,
500	                    diff_class=DiffClass.UNREPRODUCIBLE,
501	                    action=action,
502	                    item_id=item.item_id,
503	                    label=item.label,
504	                    detail=None,
505	                )
506	            )
507	        all_diffs = tuple(diffs)
508	        groups = self._build_review_groups(all_diffs)
509	        return PackagePlan(manager=self.manager_id, diffs=all_diffs, groups=groups)
510	
511	    @override
512	    def _build_review_groups(self, diffs: Sequence[ItemDiff]) -> tuple[ReviewGroup, ...]:
513	        """Carve still-unresolved `UNREPRODUCIBLE` diffs (`action=REPORT_ONLY`, D-21) into
514	        their own `UNREPRODUCIBLE_REVIEW_ACTION` group, presented after any resolved
515	        (snippet-backed, `action=INSTALL`) install group so the user sees resolved items
516	        before being asked to resolve the rest. A snippet-backed diff is NOT pulled out —

1	"""`apt_sync`: apt package convergence — install, remove, and the full diff taxonomy
2	(D-01, D-03, D-04, D-07, D-24, D-25, ADR-020).
3	
4	Captures the source's `apt-mark showmanual` set with `dpkg-query`-sourced versions
5	(never `apt list --installed` — its own manpage says the output has no stable scripting
6	contract), diffs it against the same query on the target into every D-25 class this
7	manager produces (`_diff_apt_packages`, this module's own — the base class holds no diff
8	for anyone to inherit, D-15), and converges the approved `INSTALL`/`REMOVE` items via
9	`apt-get install`/`apt-get remove`.
10	
11	A package is matched by (name, ORIGIN), never by name alone (ADR-020 D-34). The target
12	having a candidate for a name is not evidence it can supply the source's software: one name
13	is often offered by two vendors, and Ubuntu's `firefox` carries epoch 1, which outranks
14	every unpinned vendor version, so an install matched by name replicates the name and
15	inverts the provenance. `plan()` therefore reads where the source installed each package
16	from, maps that back to the repository file on the SOURCE that declares it, and classifies
17	the package against the target's real candidate origins: same origin -> ordinary install;
18	different or absent origin with a writable declaring file -> install, with that repository
19	derived from the package's own approval; no writable declaring file -> `REPO_UNAVAILABLE`,
20	reported rather than installed from somewhere else. A package installed on both machines
21	from two different vendors is `ORIGIN_MISMATCH`, report-only.
22	
23	That classification is not the guarantee — it is only what decides which repository work to
24	derive. The guarantee is `_origin_refusal` (D-35): after this run's single `apt-get update`
25	and before its first install, ONE batched `apt-cache policy` re-reads the target's candidate
26	origins, and an approved install apt would now satisfy from none of the source's origins
27	fails as its own item (D-27), naming both. It sees the state the derivation actually
28	produced, so a repository whose write failed or a pin that never landed is caught there
29	rather than shipping the wrong vendor's package. Packages the source has only from its own
30	distribution files are exempt: two machines on different Ubuntu mirrors are one vendor.
31	
32	That refusal is for a request that is wrong, which is per-item. A probe that did not run at
33	all is a different thing and gets a different answer: `_require_apt_answer` fails the run
34	once, naming the command, rather than blaming N packages' provenance for a transient
35	network, an apt lock or an interrupted dpkg.
36	
37	Bare-`.deb` packages are NOT in scope and are dropped at capture
38	(`capture_source_items`). A package whose installed version comes from no configured
39	repository was put there with `dpkg --install`; apt cannot install it on the target, and
40	`manual_installs_sync` offers it as an install snippet in the same run (D-18). Both jobs
41	compute the predicate from the shared `packages/apt_policy.py` parser — the same test, never
42	a result passed between them, since D-15/D-16 keep the four jobs independent.
43	
44	The ownership split has a consequence this job may not paper over: `manual_installs_sync`
45	has its own enable flag, and reading another job's flag is exactly the coupling D-15
46	forbids. So enabling `apt_sync` while disabling `manual_installs_sync` leaves these packages
47	replicated by nobody — silently absent rather than offered as installs that fail. Documented
48	for the user in `docs/jobs/package-sync.md`.
49	
50	Every approved item's transaction is simulated with `apt-get --dry-run` before the real
51	command runs, guarding against apt silently doing more than the review showed. Collateral
52	effects are classified by provenance (D-30): a package the simulation would remove or
53	downgrade that is auto-installed (not in the target's `apt-mark showmanual` set) is apt
54	resolving its own dependencies and proceeds silently, while a manually-installed one is
55	something the user chose to have and is refused unless the user approved losing it. `plan()`
56	runs two BATCHED simulations (the whole install candidate set, the whole removal candidate
57	set — not one per-package, which would cost more than the sync itself for 150 packages) and
58	classifies their collateral against the target manual set, emitting a three-way
59	install-anyway / skip / abort review item for each manual-collateral package so the decision
60	is made in the batched review, never as a prompt during apply. A batch that turns up manual
61	collateral then rehearses each candidate alone, so `skip` cancels the packages that actually
62	cause the collateral rather than everything the user was reviewing (`_collateral_for`).
63	
64	One install is admitted to no plan-time rehearsal at all (`_target_resolvable`, D-40): a
65	D-34 class-3 package, whose repository this run derives from its own approval and writes
66	during converge. Until that write lands the target's apt has never heard the name and
67	`apt-get --dry-run` refuses the WHOLE batch containing it, which would strip the protection
68	from every other package in the run rather than weaken it for one. The exclusion keys on the
69	target's own `apt-cache policy`, never on the simulation's exit code, which cannot separate
70	"unable to locate" from a held dpkg lock (ADR-022 D-01). What covers those packages instead
71	is the per-item rehearsal `_converge_install` runs after the group has converged, where apt
72	CAN resolve them: unapproved manual collateral fails that one item, so the user is told
73	afterwards rather than asked beforehand.
74	
75	The same plan-time-classification rule covers the `/etc/apt` removal direction (C26): a
76	source file offered for deletion because the source machine no longer has it carries, in
77	its review `detail`, the machine-specific packages the target still installs from that
78	repository. Those packages are recorded skip-always, so `filter_inert` keeps them out of
79	the target manifest and they produce no diff of their own in any run; without this the
80	review shows a bare file deletion and nothing else. Disclosure, not refusal: removing a
81	repository whose packages are going too is legitimate, so the removal stays offered (and,
82	like every removal group, unticked).
83	
84	Neither is `/etc/apt` itself, in most directions. Only what the user has a basis to judge
85	is an item (ADR-020 D-37): a repository REMOVAL, a pin REMOVAL, and apt config in all
86	three directions. Everything else under `/etc/apt` is derived and written without a
87	question, in three buckets `_build_derived_writes` assembles from the accepted decisions:
88	
89	- the repository files serving the packages the user approved (ruling 4 — a repository
90	  that feeds no package this run syncs does not travel at all);
91	- every `/etc/apt/preferences.d` file the source has, always. A pin decides which origin
92	  wins, which is precisely what origin replication turns on, and one naming an origin the
93	  target does not have is inert — so always-sync costs nothing and cannot derive wrongly;
94	- the distribution's own source files — `ubuntu.sources`, the two `ubuntu-esm-*` files and
95	  `/etc/apt/sources.list` — written when missing and overwritten when different, never
96	  removed and never offered for removal (D-38).
97	
98	The two `ubuntu-esm-*` files carry the one question this job asks that is not about an item
99	(`_gate_esm_writes`, D-38). Writing them to a target with no Ubuntu Pro attachment is not
100	harmless: `esm.ubuntu.com` serves its INDEX publicly, so the refresh succeeds and the ESM
101	suites win candidate selection, and the failure surfaces much later as a 401 on the `.deb`
102	of the target's next install of an ESM-covered package — a failure nobody traces back to a
103	sync. pc-switcher cannot attach the target itself (`pro attach` needs a subscription token
104	or a browser flow, and a machine's own credentials are root-only and not reusable), so it
105	asks, with exactly two answers: attach now, which RE-PROBES rather than trusting the answer
106	and may be given any number of times, or skip `apt_sync` for this run while every other job
107	runs. A run with nobody to ask takes the skip; a dry run warns instead. Skipping the whole
108	job rather than withholding the two files is the only coherent partial outcome, because
109	`preferences.d` always-syncs with no derivation predicate and the source's ESM pins would
110	land regardless. The gate sits in `plan()`, right after `_capture_origin_state` supplies the
111	digests its trigger reads and before any review group is built: one answer ends the job, so
112	it must precede the planning and the review the user would otherwise answer for nothing.
113	Only the parsed `attached` boolean ever leaves `_target_pro_attached` — the probe's payload
114	names the subscriber's account.
115	
116	A derived write has no item, so it cannot fail as one. It is recorded against its
117	destination and charged to every approved package whose origin depended on it (D-39):
118	the refusal lands on the thing the user actually decided about, naming the file. A rollback
119	marks every derived write failed, exactly as it already does every reviewed group item.
120	
121	A signing key is NOT an item either. It has no `ItemClass`, no `item_id`, no diff, no
122	review entry and no decision-file identity: the user thinks in repositories and packages,
123	and a key is only how a repository is made to work. Keys are two plain file operations
124	bracketing the repository group:
125	
126	- `_provision_keyrings` runs BEFORE any source file is written. It copies every source
127	  `/etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d` key the target lacks or differs on, and the keyrings named by
128	  the source files this run actually writes (a repository this run overwrites may point at
129	  a keyring the target has never seen). `_keyring_gap` still refuses to write a source
130	  whose keyring did not arrive, so a repository is never written ahead of its key — and
131	  that refusal, like every other derived-write failure, is charged to the package.
132	  Provisioning is ownership-aware in ONE direction: a keyring the target LACKS is copied
133	  whatever owns it on the source, but a keyring the target already has with different bytes
134	  is left alone when the target's own dpkg owns that path — the target's package manages
135	  that file and clobbering a distro keyring is not this job's business. Ownership must not
136	  gate the COPY, because a vendor `.deb` (`code`, `tailscale-archive-keyring`) ships both
137	  its `sources.list.d` entry and its keyring, so the repository the package comes from
138	  cannot be trusted until the key that package owns is already there; skipping
139	  package-owned keys would make that bootstrap unsatisfiable. Every derived write is
140	  logged at FULL as it lands, and previewed under `--dry-run` (ADR-014), which is how a
141	  file with no review entry stays visible without becoming a question.
142	
143	Three key directories are captured, not two: `/etc/apt/keyrings`, `/etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d`
144	and `/usr/share/keyrings`. The last is where `add-apt-repository`, several vendor `.deb`s
145	and Ubuntu itself put keyrings, and most real `Signed-By:` values point there; leaving it
146	out made every such reference resolve to nothing and downgraded the repository to
147	`REPORT_ONLY`. Like `/etc/apt/keyrings` it is provisioned only for keys a source actually
148	references, and unlike it, it is never collected: it is package territory.
149	- `_remove_unused_keyrings` runs AFTER every source write and deletion, and only when this
150	  run actually removed a source file. It re-scans the target's REAL source files and drops
151	  each `/etc/apt/keyrings` file no surviving source references. Counting against the
152	  post-write state is what makes the hard cases come out right: a repository this run
153	  deleted stops counting as a reference, while one the user left unticked, one recorded
154	  machine-specific, and one pc-switcher never syncs at all (`/etc/apt/sources.list`) all
155	  keep counting.
156	
157	Legacy `/etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d` keys are replicated but never collected: they are ambient
158	trust with no discoverable referent, so "unused" is not computable for them and they are
159	allowed to accumulate rather than be deleted on a guess.
160	
161	Keys travel byte-for-byte and are never re-fetched from a vendor (D-12).
162	
163	This job reviews EXACTLY ONCE per run, before its first mutating command (ADR-020 D-24).
164	Nothing this run writes can invalidate a decision it already took: a package is classified
165	from the SOURCE's origins, which no run mutates, and the one fact
166	that genuinely depends on the target's post-write state — which origin actually wins — is
167	not guessed at plan time at all, it is read back by `_origin_refusal` and turned into a
168	per-item refusal rather than a question.
169	
170	That is also why a pin says nothing about the packages it names (D-25). A per-package
171	"pinned" report would fire for every package a target-side `preferences.d` stanza names,
172	turning a no-op into review noise and — worse — making a package present only on the target

174	`EXTRA_ON_TARGET` diff) and impossible to silence (a `REPORT_ONLY` item cannot be recorded
175	skip-always). Pins themselves DO replicate, as FILES under `/etc/apt/preferences.d`, and
176	that is the whole mechanism: a report about them was never part of it.

420	def _display_origin(uri: str) -> str:
421	    """A repository URI in the form the review shows it (ruling 9): the FULL path with its
422	    scheme stripped — `ppa.launchpadcontent.net/git-core/ppa/ubuntu`.
423	
424	    The path, never the bare host: one Launchpad host serves thousands of unrelated PPAs and
425	    one vendor host often serves several channels, so a hostname does not identify the
426	    repository the package actually came from. Only the display strips; the comparison form
427	    stays exactly what `normalise_repo_uri` produces, scheme included, because that is what
428	    apt prints and what the two machines' URIs are matched on.

433	def build_origin_detail(origins: Sequence[str]) -> str | None:
434	    """Detail naming where an approved install would come from, or `None` when there is
435	    nothing worth naming (ruling 9).
436	
437	    `origins` is the package's NON-distribution origins, already filtered by the caller
438	    against the origins that machine's own distribution files declare — so an empty sequence
439	    means the distribution's archive serves it, which is the unremarkable case and earns no
440	    text. Several are named comma-separated and sorted, because a package genuinely served
441	    by two vendors is a fact the user should see whole.
442	    """
443	    if not origins:
444	        return None
445	    return f"from {', '.join(_display_origin(uri) for uri in origins)}"

448	def build_repo_unavailable_detail(name: str, origins: Sequence[str], cause: str) -> str:
449	    """Detail for a `REPO_UNAVAILABLE` diff: where the source has this package from, and why
450	    the target cannot be given the same place (ADR-020 D-34).
451	
452	    Both halves are load-bearing. Naming the origin is what stops this reading as "apt has
453	    never heard of it"; naming the cause is what tells the user whether the remedy is theirs
454	    (a repository file that no longer exists, a missing signing key) or nobody's.
455	    """
456	    where = f" from {', '.join(_display_origin(uri) for uri in origins)}" if origins else ""
457	    return f"{name} cannot be installed{where} on the target: {cause}"

460	def build_origin_mismatch_detail(source_origins: Sequence[str], target_origins: Sequence[str]) -> str:
461	    """Detail for an `ORIGIN_MISMATCH` diff: the same package, two vendors.
462	
463	    Report only, and both sides are named because neither is wrong — converging it would
464	    mean a cross-vendor reinstall, which is not a float (D-04) and not something the user
465	    asked for. The user is the only one who can say which machine is the odd one out.
466	    """
467	    source = ", ".join(_display_origin(uri) for uri in source_origins)
468	    target = ", ".join(_display_origin(uri) for uri in target_origins)
469	    return f"source installed it from {source}, target from {target}"
470	
471	
472	def build_origin_refusal_detail(name: str, source_origins: Sequence[str], target_origins: Sequence[str]) -> str:
473	    """Why an approved install was refused at the last moment (ADR-020 D-35): the origin the
474	    source uses, and the origin the target's apt would have installed from instead.
475	
476	    Both are named because either half alone is unactionable. "The wrong vendor" does not
477	    say which repository failed to land; "no candidate from packages.mozilla.org" does not
478	    say what the target would have shipped in its place. Together they are the whole finding,
479	    on the item the user actually decided about.
480	    """
481	    wanted = ", ".join(_display_origin(uri) for uri in source_origins)
482	    if target_origins:
483	        instead = f"would install it from {', '.join(_display_origin(uri) for uri in target_origins)}"
484	    else:
485	        instead = "offers it from no repository at all"
486	    return (
487	        f"install of {name} refused: the source has it from {wanted}, but after this run's "
488	        f"apt-get update the target {instead} (ADR-020 D-35)"
489	    )

519	class _OriginOutcome(StrEnum):
520	    """What the origin facts say can be done about one package missing on the target.
521	
522	    Three outcomes, not ADR-020 D-34's four: its classes 2 and 3 (the target has a candidate
523	    from the wrong vendor / the target has no candidate at all) differ only in what they
524	    look like, never in what happens — both install the package and both derive the source's
525	    repository first — so collapsing them keeps the diff from branching on a distinction
526	    that has no consequence.
527	    """
528	
529	    SAME_ORIGIN = "same_origin"
530	    """Class 1. Ordinary install, zero repository work — the target already offers the
531	    package from a place the source uses, or there is no origin fact to hold it to."""
532	
533	    REPLICABLE = "replicable"
534	    """Classes 2 and 3. Install, with the source's repository files derived from it."""
535	
536	    UNREPLICABLE = "unreplicable"
537	    """Class 4. `REPO_UNAVAILABLE`/`REPORT_ONLY` — the origin is declared by no writable
538	    file on the source, so the package can only be reported."""
539
