541	@dataclass(frozen=True)
542	class _OriginPlan:
543	    """Every origin fact one source package's classification turns on (ADR-020 D-34).
544	
545	    Assembled per package in `plan()` from facts about BOTH machines, because the question
546	    "can the target end up with this package from the same place the source has it?" is not
547	    answerable from either machine alone.
548	    """
549	
550	    source_origins: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
551	    """Origin URIs of the package's INSTALLED version on the source. Empty means apt named
552	    none for it, or printed no block at all — never evidence of anything (`df48cd07`)."""
553	
554	    source_files: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
555	    """The source's repository files declaring any of `source_origins`. Computed only for a
556	    package missing on the target, which is the only case that could make one travel."""
557	
558	    target_candidate_origins: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
559	    """Origin URIs of the version the TARGET would install. Empty means no repository on
560	    the target offers the name."""
561	
562	    target_candidate_known: bool = False
563	    """Whether apt printed a block for the name on the target AT ALL. Silence is not the
564	    same answer as `Candidate: (none)` and must never be read as one (`df48cd07`): the
565	    first is a question apt did not answer, including the case where the whole command
566	    failed; only the second is apt saying it will install nothing."""
567	
568	    vendor_source_origins: tuple[str, ...] = ()
569	    """`source_origins` minus the SOURCE's distribution origins, sorted. What the review
570	    names (ruling 9), and the left-hand side of the provenance comparison (§2.6)."""
571	
572	    vendor_target_origins: tuple[str, ...] = ()
573	    """The package's INSTALLED origins on the target minus the TARGET's distribution
574	    origins, sorted. Filtered against the target's own distribution files so two machines
575	    on different Ubuntu mirrors do not read as two vendors."""
576	
577	    unwritable: str | None = None
578	    """Why no file serving `source_origins` can be written on the target, or `None` when at
579	    least one can. A file whose `Signed-By:` resolves to no key on the source is a
580	    repository apt would refuse on the target, so it cannot deliver the origin."""
581	
582	    def outcome(self) -> _OriginOutcome:
583	        """Which of ADR-020 D-34's outcomes this package falls into.
584	
585	        The ladder is ordered by what it takes to be sure: a target candidate from an origin
586	        the source uses settles the question outright, and only after that does it matter
587	        whether the origin could be replicated at all.
588	        """
589	        if not self.source_origins:
590	            # apt named no repository origin for the source's installed version, or printed
591	            # no block for it at all. Absence is never evidence (`df48cd07`): with no origin
592	            # to replicate there is nothing to compare, so the question degrades to the
593	            # presence one this job asked before origins existed — and on that question the
594	            # target's silence still condemns nothing, only an explicit `Candidate: (none)`
595	            # does. A run whose policy call failed proposes the install and lets the install
596	            # report its own failure, rather than reporting a repository problem it never
597	            # established.
598	            refused = self.target_candidate_known and not self.target_candidate_origins
599	            return _OriginOutcome.UNREPLICABLE if refused else _OriginOutcome.SAME_ORIGIN
600	        if self.source_origins & self.target_candidate_origins:
601	            return _OriginOutcome.SAME_ORIGIN
602	        if self.source_files and self.unwritable is None:
603	            return _OriginOutcome.REPLICABLE
604	        return _OriginOutcome.UNREPLICABLE
605	
606	    @property
607	    def derived_files(self) -> frozenset[str]:
608	        """The source repository files approving this package would make travel (ruling 4).
609	
610	        Empty for `SAME_ORIGIN`: the target already offers the package from a place the
611	        source uses, so nothing about `/etc/apt` has to change for the install to be
612	        faithful. Empty for `UNREPLICABLE` too — that package is reported, not installed,
613	        and deriving a repository for a report-only item would break ruling 4's "derived
614	        from the packages approved from it".
615	        """
616	        return self.source_files if self.outcome() is _OriginOutcome.REPLICABLE else frozenset()
617	
618	    @property
619	    def unavailable_cause(self) -> str:
620	        """Why the source's origin cannot be provided on the target — the second half of a
621	        `REPO_UNAVAILABLE` detail, after the origin itself.
622	        """
623	        if self.unwritable is not None:
624	            return self.unwritable
625	        if not self.source_origins:
626	            return "the source's apt names no repository origin for it"
627	        return "no repository file on the source declares it"
628

632	    """One batched `apt-cache policy` on the target, parsed for every question this run asks
633	    of it — never one call per question, and never one call per package.
634	
635	    The installed and the candidate rows are different rows and answer different questions
636	    (`apt_policy` module docstring): the candidate says what the target WOULD install, the
637	    installed says where what it already has came from.
638	    """
639	
640	    candidate_origins: Mapping[str, frozenset[str]] = field(default_factory=dict)
641	    installed_origins: Mapping[str, frozenset[str]] = field(default_factory=dict)

644	def _is_origin_mismatch(plan: _OriginPlan) -> bool:
645	    """Whether a package present on BOTH machines came from two different vendors (§2.6).
646	
647	    Both sides must name a vendor and the two sets must not overlap. A side with no vendor
648	    origin at all is served by the distribution, and the distribution is not a vendor — that
649	    suppression is the whole reason this can be asked of every package without two machines
650	    on different Ubuntu mirrors reporting every one of them as mismatched.
651	    """
652	    return (
653	        bool(plan.vendor_source_origins)
654	        and bool(plan.vendor_target_origins)
655	        and not (frozenset(plan.vendor_source_origins) & frozenset(plan.vendor_target_origins))
656	    )

658	
659	def _diff_apt_packages(
660	    source_items: Sequence[AptPackageItem],
661	    target_items: Sequence[AptPackageItem],
662	    origin_plan: Mapping[str, _OriginPlan],
663	    source_hold_names: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
664	    target_hold_names: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
665	) -> list[ItemDiff]:
666	    """One diff per item id present on either side, source-then-target order,
667	    followed by the `apt:hold:` membership diffs (#208, D5/D8 — holds emitted AFTER
668	    package diffs so install lands before its hold once the diffs converge).
669	
670	    A HELD package (target hold set) has its install/upgrade action SUPPRESSED (a held
671	    package is never proposed for install/version change) but produces NO package-level
672	    report — the hold travels as its own `apt:hold:` item, so a held package is never
673	    double-reported. A PINNED package gets no echo of any kind: a pin's only job is
674	    deciding which origin wins, which D-35 checks against the target's real post-refresh
675	    state instead of guessing at it here. Otherwise:
676	
677	    - missing-on-target -> `MISSING_ON_TARGET`/`INSTALL` when the source's origin either
678	      already serves the target or can be made to (`_OriginPlan.outcome`), else
679	      `REPO_UNAVAILABLE`/`REPORT_ONLY`. This is ADR-020 D-34: the package a target could
680	      satisfy from a DIFFERENT vendor is still an install, but one that carries the source's
681	      repository with it, and the review line names where it will come from.
682	    - extra-on-target -> `EXTRA_ON_TARGET`/`REMOVE`.
683	    - present on both, from vendors that do not overlap -> `ORIGIN_MISMATCH`/`REPORT_ONLY`,
684	      checked BEFORE the version comparison: two vendors' copies of one name have no common
685	      version scale, so "source has X, target has Y" would report a difference of degree
686	      where the real difference is of provenance.
687	    - present on both with differing versions -> `VERSION_MISMATCH`/`REPORT_ONLY` (D-04:
688	      reported, never force-downgraded).
689	    - present on both, same vendor, same version -> no diff at all.
690	
691	    Hold membership (D2): source-held & target-not -> `AptHoldItem` INSTALL (hold);
692	    target-held & source-not -> REMOVE (unhold); held on both or neither -> no diff.
693	    """
694	    source_by_id = {item.item_id: item for item in source_items}
695	    target_by_id = {item.item_id: item for item in target_items}
696	
697	    seen: dict[str, None] = {}
698	    for item in (*source_items, *target_items):
699	        seen.setdefault(item.item_id, None)
700	
701	    diffs: list[ItemDiff] = []
702	    for item_id in seen:
703	        source_item = source_by_id.get(item_id)
704	        target_item = target_by_id.get(item_id)
705	
706	        if target_item is not None and target_item.name in target_hold_names:
707	            # Held on the target: suppress its install/version action entirely (a held
708	            # package must never be proposed for install/upgrade). No package-level
709	            # report — the `apt:hold:` item below carries the hold fact.
710	            continue
711	        elif source_item is not None and target_item is None:
712	            origins = origin_plan.get(item_id, _OriginPlan())
713	            if origins.outcome() is _OriginOutcome.UNREPLICABLE:
714	                diffs.append(
715	                    ItemDiff(
716	                        item_class=ItemClass.APT_PACKAGE,
717	                        diff_class=DiffClass.REPO_UNAVAILABLE,
718	                        action=DiffAction.REPORT_ONLY,
719	                        item_id=item_id,
720	                        label=source_item.label(),
721	                        detail=build_repo_unavailable_detail(
722	                            source_item.name, sorted(origins.source_origins), origins.unavailable_cause
723	                        ),
724	                    )
725	                )
726	            else:
727	                diffs.append(
728	                    ItemDiff(
729	                        item_class=ItemClass.APT_PACKAGE,
730	                        diff_class=DiffClass.MISSING_ON_TARGET,
731	                        action=DiffAction.INSTALL,
732	                        item_id=item_id,
733	                        label=source_item.label(),
734	                        detail=build_origin_detail(origins.vendor_source_origins),
735	                    )
736	                )
737	        elif target_item is not None and source_item is None:
738	            diffs.append(
739	                ItemDiff(
740	                    item_class=ItemClass.APT_PACKAGE,
741	                    diff_class=DiffClass.EXTRA_ON_TARGET,
742	                    action=DiffAction.REMOVE,
743	                    item_id=item_id,
744	                    label=target_item.label(),
745	                    detail=None,
746	                )
747	            )
748	        elif _is_origin_mismatch(origin_plan.get(item_id, _OriginPlan())):
749	            origins = origin_plan[item_id]
750	            diffs.append(
751	                ItemDiff(
752	                    item_class=ItemClass.APT_PACKAGE,
753	                    diff_class=DiffClass.ORIGIN_MISMATCH,
754	                    action=DiffAction.REPORT_ONLY,
755	                    item_id=item_id,

779	def _diff_apt_holds(source_hold_names: frozenset[str], target_hold_names: frozenset[str]) -> list[ItemDiff]:
780	    """`apt:hold:` membership diffs (#208, D2): source-held & target-not -> INSTALL
781	    (hold); target-held & source-not -> REMOVE (unhold); held on both or on neither
782	    -> no diff. `sorted` for a stable, deterministic review order.
783	    """
784	    diffs: list[ItemDiff] = []
785	    for name in sorted(source_hold_names | target_hold_names):
786	        in_source = name in source_hold_names
787	        in_target = name in target_hold_names
788	        if in_source == in_target:
789	            continue
790	        hold_item = AptHoldItem(name=name)
791	        diffs.append(
792	            ItemDiff(
793	                item_class=ItemClass.APT_HOLD,
794	                diff_class=DiffClass.MISSING_ON_TARGET if in_source else DiffClass.EXTRA_ON_TARGET,
795	                action=DiffAction.INSTALL if in_source else DiffAction.REMOVE,
796	                item_id=hold_item.item_id,
797	                label=hold_item.label(),
798	                detail=None,
799	            )
800	        )
801	    return diffs

890	async def compare_deb_versions(executor: Executor, left: str, right: str) -> int:
891	    """Compare two Debian package version strings, `sorted`-comparator convention.
892	
893	    Returns negative when `left` < `right`, zero when equal, positive when `left` >
894	    `right`. Not hand-rolled: Debian version ordering has epoch, tilde and revision
895	    tie-breaking rules that are neither lexicographic nor PEP 440 — only dpkg's own
896	    comparator correctly ranks an epoch-bearing version like `2:1.0` above `10.0`
897	    (RESEARCH Don't Hand-Roll). Shells out through `executor` (never assumes a local
898	    `dpkg`, since the target's version may need comparing against its own dpkg) with
899	    `shlex.quote` on both operands (ASVS V5, T-02-01). Short-circuits to equal for
900	    byte-identical strings so the common "nothing changed" case costs no subprocess.
901	    """
902	    if left == right:
903	        return 0
904	
905	    quoted_left = shlex.quote(left)
906	    quoted_right = shlex.quote(right)
907	
908	    lt_result = await executor.run_command(f"dpkg --compare-versions {quoted_left} lt {quoted_right}")
909	    if lt_result.success:
910	        return -1
911	
912	    gt_result = await executor.run_command(f"dpkg --compare-versions {quoted_left} gt {quoted_right}")
913	    if gt_result.success:
914	        return 1
915	
916	    return 0

988	# -- Repository/key/pin/config capture and diff (D-11, D-12, D-13) ---------------------
989	#
990	# Unlike apt packages, these five directories are diffed by whole-FILE digest (module
991	# docstring, RESEARCH's alternatives table): one batched `sha256sum` listing per
992	# directory tells us which filenames differ without transferring a single byte, and the
993	# full content of a file is only fetched for the files a diff actually implicates
994	# (missing-on-target, extra-on-target, or digest-mismatched) — never for a file that is
995	# already identical on both machines.
996	
997	_SIGNED_BY_RE = re.compile(r"^Signed-By:\s*(?P<path>\S+)", re.IGNORECASE)
998	_LEGACY_SIGNED_BY_RE = re.compile(r"signed-by=(?P<path>[^\]\s,]+)")
999	
1000

1001	def _keyring_reference(value: str) -> str | None:
1002	    """`value` as a keyring PATH reference, or `None` when it is not one.
1003	
1004	    A `Signed-By:` field carries either a path or an INLINE armored key. Only an absolute
1005	    path is a reference to a file that has to exist; anything else is the armored block
1006	    itself and needs no provisioning, because it travels inside the source file. The
1007	    distinction is not cosmetic: `add-apt-repository` writes the armor's first line on the
1008	    field line (`Signed-By: -----BEGIN PGP PUBLIC KEY BLOCK-----`), so a bare `\\S+` capture
1009	    turns every PPA added the normal way into a reference to a file named `-----BEGIN`,
1010	    which resolves nowhere and downgrades the repository to `REPORT_ONLY`.
1011	    """
1012	    return value if value.startswith("/") else None
1013	
1014	
1015	# A deb822 stanza's repository URIs (one field, possibly several space-separated values,
1016	# and one file may hold several stanzas), and a legacy `.list` line's single URI — which
1017	# sits after the optional `[opt=val ...]` bracket, so the bracket must be consumed rather
1018	# than treated as the URI.
1019	_URIS_RE = re.compile(r"^URIs:\s*(?P<uris>.+)$", re.IGNORECASE)
1020	_LEGACY_DEB_LINE_RE = re.compile(r"^deb(?:-src)?\s+(?:\[[^\]]*\]\s*)?(?P<uri>\S+)")
1021	
1022	
1023	def _parse_sha256sum(output: str) -> dict[str, str]:
1024	    """`<digest>  <path>` lines (one per `sha256sum` invocation) -> `{basename: digest}`.
1025	
1026	    Basename, not the full path: every caller already knows which directory it asked
1027	    about, and item identity is the filename (module docstring), not the path.
1028	    """
1029	    digests: dict[str, str] = {}
1030	    for line in _lines(output):
1031	        parts = line.split(None, 1)
1032	        if len(parts) != 2:
1033	            continue
1034	        digest, path = parts
1035	        digests[Path(path).name] = digest
1036	    return digests

1039	def _parse_source_file(
1040	    filename: str, content: str
1041	) -> tuple[Literal["deb822", "list"], tuple[str, ...], tuple[str, ...]]:
1042	    """A source file's format (by extension), every keyring path it names, and every
1043	    repository URI it points at (normalised by `normalise_repo_uri`).
1044	
1045	    deb822 `.sources` files name a key via a `Signed-By:` field and their repositories via
1046	    `URIs:`; legacy `.list` files put both on the `deb` line, the key inside the options
1047	    bracket as `[... signed-by=<path> ...]` and the URI immediately after it (RESEARCH
1048	    Standard Stack). Parsed just far enough to extract these — never rewritten,
1049	    normalised, or migrated between formats (RESEARCH Pitfall 3, deferred ideas).
1050	
1051	    One parser, three consumers: the keyring refs drive D-12's dangling-reference check
1052	    and keyring garbage collection, the URIs drive the source-removal impact (C26) by
1053	    matching against the origin `apt-cache policy` reports for an installed package.
1054	
1055	    A `Signed-By:` field may carry an INLINE armored key instead of a path, either with an
1056	    empty field value and the block on continuation lines or with the block's first line on
1057	    the field line itself. Neither yields a ref (`_keyring_reference`), which is correct in
1058	    both directions: the file depends on no key FILE, so nothing is invented for it, and no
1059	    part of the armored block is mistaken for a path.
1060	    """
1061	    fmt: Literal["deb822", "list"] = "deb822" if filename.endswith(".sources") else "list"
1062	    refs: list[str] = []
1063	    uris: list[str] = []
1064	    for raw_line in content.splitlines():
1065	        line = raw_line.strip()
1066	        if fmt == "deb822":
1067	            signed_by = _SIGNED_BY_RE.match(line)
1068	            uri_field = _URIS_RE.match(line)
1069	            if uri_field:
1070	                uris.extend(normalise_repo_uri(uri) for uri in uri_field.group("uris").split())
1071	        else:
1072	            signed_by = _LEGACY_SIGNED_BY_RE.search(raw_line)
1073	            deb_line = _LEGACY_DEB_LINE_RE.match(line)
1074	            if deb_line:
1075	                uris.append(normalise_repo_uri(deb_line.group("uri")))
1076	        if signed_by:
1077	            ref = _keyring_reference(signed_by.group("path"))
1078	            if ref is not None:
1079	                refs.append(ref)
1080	    return fmt, tuple(refs), tuple(uris)

1083	def _dangling_keyring_ref(keyring_refs: Sequence[str], source_key_filenames: frozenset[str]) -> str | None:
1084	    """The first `keyring_refs` entry whose basename is absent from
1085	    `source_key_filenames`, or `None` if every reference resolves to a real file on the
1086	    source. A source file with no `Signed-By:`/`signed-by=` at all (`keyring_refs` is
1087	    empty) has nothing to validate — it is not itself a dangling reference.

1090	    dangling only when the source machine really has no such key — not merely when it keeps
1091	    it somewhere this job did not think to look.
1092	    """
1093	    for ref in keyring_refs:
1094	        if Path(ref).name not in source_key_filenames:

1099	async def _capture_dir_digests(
1100	    run: Callable[[str], Awaitable[CommandResult]],
1101	    directory: str,
1102	    host: Host,
1103	    *,
1104	    extensions: Sequence[str] = (),
1105	) -> dict[str, str]:
1106	    """One `if sudo test -d <dir>; then sudo find <dir> -maxdepth 1 -type f -exec sha256sum
1107	    {} +; fi` per directory — a single batched command, never one `sha256sum` per file.
1108	    `-exec ... {} +` never runs at all when the directory has no matching files, so an empty
1109	    directory degrades to an empty digest map rather than a shell error.
1110	
1111	    `extensions` narrows the capture to the files apt itself reads, and is only correct
1112	    where apt HAS such a rule: `sources.list.d` is read for `*.list`/`*.sources` alone, so
1113	    the `.save`/`.curtin.orig` copies apt ignores must not become syncable items.
1114	    `preferences.d` and `apt.conf.d` pass no extensions, because apt reads extensionless
1115	    files in both.
1116	
1117	    An ABSENT directory is a separate case and is what the `sudo test -d` wrapper is for
1118	    (ADR-022). Measured: `find` on a path that does not exist exits 1, exactly as it does
1119	    when it cannot read one that does — so without the wrapper the two would be one signal,
1120	    and the only ways to resolve it are both wrong. Failing every run on a machine with no
1121	    `/etc/apt/preferences.d` turns a legitimate "no pins here" into an error; accepting the
1122	    exit code turns a directory this run could not read into "that machine has no
1123	    repositories", which offers every file on the other machine for removal. With the
1124	    wrapper an absent directory answers "nothing" at exit 0 and a non-zero exit is only
1125	    ever a real failure, which `require_answer` then fails the job on.
1126	
1127	    The test runs under `sudo` for the same WR-04 reason the `find` does, and the two must
1128	    stay at the same privilege: measured, an unprivileged `test -d` on a directory inside an
1129	    unsearchable parent exits 1, which collapses the whole `if` to exit 0 with no output —
1130	    the reshape's one failure mode, answering "this machine has no pins or keys" for a
1131	    directory root would have listed.
1132	    """
1133	    quoted = shlex.quote(directory)
1134	    predicate = ""
1135	    if extensions:
1136	        names = " -o ".join(f"-name {shlex.quote(f'*{ext}')}" for ext in extensions)
1137	        predicate = f"\\( {names} \\) "
1138	    command = (
1139	        f"if sudo test -d {quoted}; then sudo find {quoted} -maxdepth 1 -type f {predicate}-exec sha256sum {{}} +; fi"
1140	    )
1141	    result = await run(command)
1142	    require_answer(command, result, host)
1143	    return _parse_sha256sum(result.stdout)

1150	    which is a file rather than a directory and so has no `find` listing to appear in.

1152	    absent case falls out of the parse rather than needing a probe of its own.

1172	    silence would otherwise become is file CONTENT: the repository-conflict review shows
1173	    this text as the two machines' versions of a file it is asking permission to overwrite
1174	    (ADR-020 D-37), and two empty panes are an overwrite approved off a diff nobody
1175	    could read. An empty answer at exit 0 stays data — an empty source file is a legitimate
1176	    file.

1188	async def _scan_source_file_references(
1189	    run: Callable[[str], Awaitable[CommandResult]],
1190	    host: Host,
1191	) -> dict[str, tuple[tuple[str, ...], tuple[str, ...]]]:
1192	    """`{filename: (keyring_refs, repository URIs)}` for EVERY source file on a machine,
1193	    from ONE batched command — `sources.list.d` AND `/etc/apt/sources.list`.
1194	
1195	    Machine-agnostic by construction (it takes the `run` callable and names no host), and
1196	    run against BOTH machines: the target's answer drives the two consumers below, the
1197	    source's answer is what maps a package's origin URIs back to the repository file that
1198	    would have to travel for it (ADR-020 D-34).
1199	
1200	    Two target-side consumers, both of which need a fact no diff carries. The source-removal
1201	    impact (C26) needs the repository URIs of a file whose deletion is offered. Keyring
1202	    garbage collection needs the reference count of a key across every source file that
1203	    exists, which is emphatically not the set of files any diff implicates: a keyring is
1204	    commonly named only by files that are byte-identical on both machines, or that the user
1205	    marked machine-specific, or — `/etc/apt/sources.list` — that pc-switcher never syncs at
1206	    all. Missing any of those would delete a key that is still in use.
1207	
1208	    Deliberately unfiltered by extension, unlike `_capture_dir_digests`' `sources.list.d`
1209	    capture: a keyring named only by a file apt ignores is still a key nothing else
1210	    references, and keeping it is cheaper than deleting one that turns out to be in use.
1211	
1212	    `find ... -exec awk {} +` passes every file to one awk process, never one command per
1213	    file, and awk emits only the `URIs:`/`Signed-By:`/`deb` lines rather than whole
1214	    files — so this stays compatible with the module docstring's rule that full content is
1215	    fetched only for a file a diff implicates. `sudo`-qualified to match
1216	    `_capture_dir_digests`'s privilege (WR-04): an unprivileged read of a locked-down
1217	    source file returns empty output rather than failing, which would silently report no
1218	    dependency where one exists.

1477	async def simulate_apt_transaction(
1478	    executor: RemoteExecutor, apt_args: str, *, login_shell: bool | None = False
1479	) -> AptTransactionPreview:
1480	    """Run `apt-get --dry-run <apt_args>` on `executor` and parse its Inst/Remv action lines.
1481	
1482	    No `sudo` is needed: simulation is read-only. Raises `ConvergeItemFailed` if the
1483	    simulation itself fails: a failed `apt-get --dry-run` typically prints no Inst/Remv
1484	    lines, which would otherwise parse as an indistinguishable-from-clean empty preview and
1485	    let both call sites proceed with a real command whose simulation was never actually
1486	    trustworthy (WR-01) — refuse rather than silently degrade.
1487	
1488	    `ConvergeItemFailed` and not `ProbeFailed`, which is the deliberate boundary of ADR-022
1489	    D-01: apt gives this command ONE failure code for both categories. Measured in a stock
1490	    `ubuntu:24.04`, a name apt cannot locate exits 100 with `E: Unable to locate package`,
1491	    which is byte-for-byte the exit code a held dpkg lock produces, and no rewrite of the
1492	    command's SYNTAX separates them — apt offers no second code and no second mode.
1493	
1494	    Apply time simulates one approved install or removal, where apt's refusal is a fact
1495	    about that request (ADR-020 D-27). Plan time removes the ambiguity from its ARGUMENTS
1496	    instead: it rehearses only names the target's `apt-cache policy` gave a candidate for
1497	    (`AptSyncJob._target_resolvable`), so "unable to locate" is not among the failures it
1498	    can meet. What remains there — a lock, a broken apt, an unresolvable candidate set — has
1499	    no per-item loop to be reported against, so it aborts the plan, which is correct: a
1500	    rehearsal that did not happen must not read as a clean one.
1501	    """
1502	    result = await executor.run_command(f"apt-get --dry-run {apt_args}", login_shell=login_shell)
1503	    if not result.success:
1504	        raise ConvergeItemFailed(f"apt-get --dry-run {apt_args} failed: {result.stderr.strip()}")
1505	    installs: list[str] = []
1506	    removals: list[str] = []
1507	    install_versions: dict[str, tuple[str | None, str]] = {}
1508	    for line in result.stdout.splitlines():
1509	        match = _TRANSACTION_LINE_RE.match(line)
1510	        if match is None:
1511	            continue
1512	        verb, name = match.group("verb"), match.group("name")
1513	        if verb == "Inst":
1514	            installs.append(name)
1515	            new_version = match.group("new_version")
1516	            if new_version is not None:
1517	                install_versions[name] = (match.group("old_version"), new_version)
1518	        elif verb == "Remv":
1519	            removals.append(name)
1520	    return AptTransactionPreview(
1521	        installs=tuple(installs), removals=tuple(removals), raw=result.stdout, install_versions=install_versions
1522	    )

1753	    async def _resolve_versions(
1754	        showmanual_output: str, run: Callable[[str], Awaitable[CommandResult]], host: Host
1755	    ) -> list[AptPackageItem]:
1756	        """Resolve every name's version with ONE `dpkg-query` call (RESEARCH.md).
1757	
1758	        Guarded on the exit code alone (ADR-022). A version this call fails to supply
1759	        becomes the empty string, which reads as a version difference against the other
1760	        machine and turns the whole manifest into upgrade proposals. Measured: `dpkg-query`
1761	        exits 1 when ANY queried name is unknown to dpkg and when its admin directory is
1762	        unreadable; every name here came from `apt-mark showmanual`, which lists only
1763	        installed packages (measured: a package removed without `--purge` leaves the
1764	        showmanual set), so the first case cannot arise and a non-zero exit means dpkg.
1765	        """
1766	        names = _lines(showmanual_output)
1767	        if not names:
1768	            return []
1769	
1770	        quoted = " ".join(shlex.quote(name) for name in names)
1771	        # dpkg-query, not `apt list --installed`: apt's own manpage warns the latter's
1772	        # output has no stable contract for scripting. The literal \t/\n below are
1773	        # dpkg-query's OWN format-string escapes (interpreted by dpkg-query, not the
1774	        # shell) — hence a plain (non-f) string so Python leaves them as two-char
1775	        # backslash sequences for dpkg-query to expand into real tab/newline.
1776	        versions_command = "dpkg-query --show --showformat='${Package}\\t${Version}\\n' " + quoted
1777	        versions_result = await run(versions_command)
1778	        require_answer(versions_command, versions_result, host)
1779	
1780	        versions: dict[str, str] = {}
1781	        for line in versions_result.stdout.splitlines():
1782	            if not line.strip():
1783	                continue
1784	            pkg_name, _, version = line.partition("\t")
1785	            versions[pkg_name] = version
1786	
1787	        return [AptPackageItem(name=name, version=versions.get(name, "")) for name in names]

1936	    async def plan(self) -> PackagePlan:
1937	        """Extends the base diff (missing/extra/mismatch/held/unavailable) with
1938	        plan-time apt transaction-collateral classification (D-30) and the four
1939	        `/etc/apt/*` repository item classes (D-11/D-12/D-13).
1940	
1941	        Unreproducible detection is NOT apt's business (D-18): it moved to
1942	        `manual_installs_sync` with its own enable flag, so this job never emits an
1943	        `UNREPRODUCIBLE` diff.
1944	
1945	        `_capture_origin_state` runs FIRST, ahead of the package diff: a package's diff
1946	        class depends on which repository file on the source declares its origin (D-34), so
1947	        the `/etc/apt` reference scans are an input to the package diff rather than a
1948	        by-product of the repository one.
1949	
1950	        The ESM gate (D-38) runs next, for three reasons that each rule out a later spot:
1951	        one of its answers ends the job, so it must precede the expensive planning and a
1952	        review the user would otherwise answer for nothing; its probe is a read, and this is
1953	        the last read-only phase; and it puts the target's environment problem and its
1954	        copy-paste remedy on screen before anything is approved or written. Not `validate()`
1955	        — every `ValidationError` is fatal (`orchestrator.py`, `models.py`), so there is no
1956	        way to express "the user answered, carry on".
1957	
1958	        Collateral classification runs AFTER the base diff and BEFORE review groups are
1959	        (re)built. The batched
1960	        apt-get --dry-run simulations reveal what the pending transaction would also remove or
1961	        downgrade; each such package is split by provenance against the target's
1962	        `apt-mark showmanual` set (captured here, once). An auto-installed collateral
1963	        package is apt resolving its own dependencies — it proceeds silently, producing no
1964	        review item. A manually-installed collateral package is something the user chose to
1965	        have, so it becomes its own three-way review item (install-anyway / skip / abort)
1966	        decided at plan time, in the SAME review the user approves from — never a prompt
1967	        during apply.
1968	        """
1969	        await self._capture_origin_state()
1970	        pending_esm = self._pending_esm_writes()
1971	        if pending_esm and not await self._gate_esm_writes(pending_esm):
1972	            # Dry run only (`_gate_esm_writes`): a real run has raised by now. Withholding
1973	            # keeps the preview from claiming writes no real run would make.
1974	            self._withheld_esm_sources = frozenset(pending_esm)
1975	        base_plan = await self._plan_packages()
1976	        self._target_manual_set = await self._capture_target_manual_set()
1977	        collateral_diffs = await self._collect_plan_time_collateral(base_plan.diffs)
1978	        repo_diffs = await self._plan_repo_diffs()
1979	
1980	        if not collateral_diffs and not repo_diffs and not self._repo_conflicts:
1981	            return base_plan
1982	
1983	        # Ordering is an apt FACT (key before source before packages, T-02-16), not a
1984	        # general one: the base loop stays a plain item-by-item iterator, and THIS job
1985	        # sorts its own diffs before they reach it. `sorted` is stable, so within one
1986	        # rank (e.g. every APT_PACKAGE diff, or every APT_PIN/APT_CONFIG diff) the
1987	        # original relative order — base diff, then collateral, then repo diffs — is
1988	        # preserved.
1989	        # This job's OWN extra diffs (repo files) also need the D-08a inertness pass the
1990	        # base `plan()` already ran over its diffs — they are derived from directory
1991	        # digests, so no input item carried their id into `filter_inert`. The decision

1994	            sorted(

1996	                key=lambda diff: _ITEM_CLASS_ORDER.get(diff.item_class, 3),
1997	            ),
1998	            *self._plan_decisions,

2528	    async def _collateral_for(
2529	        self,
2530	        candidates: Sequence[str],
2531	        reviewed_names: frozenset[str],
2532	        args_for: Callable[[Sequence[str]], str],
2533	        *,
2534	        verb: str,

2537	        manual collateral — the narrowing that says WHICH candidates cause each item.

2539	        Attribution matters because `skip` cancels the candidates recorded against the item
2540	        (`self._collateral_trigger_ids`): blaming the whole batch would make one collateral
2541	        question cancel every package in it, including packages whose own transaction never
2542	        touches the collateral. The batch alone cannot say — apt reports the transaction, not

2556	        if not found:
2557	            return []
2558	
2559	        triggers = {name: frozenset(candidates) for name, _ in found}
2560	        if len(candidates) > 1:
2561	            narrowed: dict[str, set[str]] = {name: set() for name, _ in found}
2562	            for candidate in candidates:
2563	                alone = await simulate_apt_transaction(self.target, args_for([candidate]), login_shell=False)

2568	
2569	        return [
2570	            self._collateral_item(
2571	                name,
2572	                f"{effect} by {verb} {_trigger_phrase(triggers[name], candidates)}",

2578	    async def _classify_collateral(
2579	        self, preview: AptTransactionPreview, reviewed_names: frozenset[str]

2581	        """Partition a simulation's would-remove/would-downgrade packages by provenance

2583	        item (ADR-020 D-40); one outside it is auto-installed — apt's own dependency — and
2584	        produces nothing, not even a report line the user cannot act on.
2585

2587	        non-`None` old version and `compare_deb_versions(target, new, old) < 0`.
2588

2590	        attribute them before the effect can be phrased — the sentence names the candidates
2591	        that cause it.

2594	        collateral: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
2595	
2596	        for pkg in preview.removals:
2597	            if pkg in reviewed_names or pkg not in protected:
2598	                continue
2599	            collateral.append((pkg, "would be removed"))
2600	
2601	        for pkg, (old_version, new_version) in preview.install_versions.items():
2602	            if pkg in reviewed_names or old_version is None or pkg not in protected:
2603	                continue
2604	            if await compare_deb_versions(self.target, new_version, old_version) < 0:
2605	                collateral.append((pkg, f"would be downgraded from {old_version} to {new_version}"))

2634	    def _resolve_collateral(self, plan: PackagePlan, outcome: ReviewOutcome) -> ReviewOutcome:
2635	        """Translate the manual-collateral group's decisions (D-30) into the guard's
2636	        approved set and the triggering installs' decisions.
2637	
2638	        For each collateral item (`apt:collateral:<pkg>`): an `APPLY` (install-anyway)
2639	        marks `<pkg>` approved, so `_converge_install`/`_converge_remove` let its removal
2640	        or downgrade through; a `SKIP_ONCE` (skip) is propagated to the packages whose own
2641	        transaction causes that collateral (`self._collateral_trigger_ids`, attributed in
2642	        `_collateral_for`), so each is cleanly left unapproved rather than attempted and
2643	        refused at the guard. Abort never reaches here — it raised `SyncAbortedByUser`
2644	        inside the review.

2647	        cancelling, and overriding a `SKIP_ALWAYS` would silently discard the "never offer
2648	        again on this machine" mark it carries: `_record_permanent_skips` reads this same
2649	        decisions map, so the mark would never be written and the user would be asked again
2650	        next run having been told otherwise.

2653	        decisions map untouched when there is no collateral to resolve.

2655	        approved: set[str] = set()
2656	        overrides: dict[str, Decision] = {}
2657	        for diff in plan.diffs:
2658	            if not _is_collateral_diff(diff):

2660	            decision = outcome.decisions.get(diff.item_id)
2661	            if decision == Decision.APPLY:
2662	                approved.add(diff.item_id.removeprefix(_COLLATERAL_ID_PREFIX))
2663	            elif decision == Decision.SKIP_ONCE:
2664	                for trigger_id in self._collateral_trigger_ids.get(diff.item_id, frozenset()):
2665	                    if outcome.decisions.get(trigger_id) == Decision.APPLY:
2666	                        overrides[trigger_id] = Decision.SKIP_ONCE
2667	
2668	        self._approved_collateral = frozenset(approved)
2669	        if not overrides:
2670	            return outcome
2671	        return ReviewOutcome(
2672	            decisions={**outcome.decisions, **overrides},
2673	            was_interactive=outcome.was_interactive,
2674	            snippets=outcome.snippets,
2675	            unresolved=outcome.unresolved,
2676	        )

2678	    def _build_derived_writes(self, plan: PackagePlan, outcome: ReviewOutcome) -> None:
2679	        """Turn the accepted decisions into the `/etc/apt` files this run writes WITHOUT a
2680	        review line (ADR-020 D-37/D-38) — the counterpart to `_approved_repo_group_diffs`,
2681	        which carries the reviewed half.
2682	
2683	        Three buckets, in the order §3.3 writes them, and each is a different answer to
2684	        "why does this file travel":
2685	
2686	        - Every `/etc/apt/preferences.d` file the source has. A pin decides which origin
2687	          wins, which is exactly what origin replication turns on; one naming an origin the
2688	          target lacks is inert, so always-sync costs nothing and cannot get a derivation
2689	          wrong.
2690	        - The distribution's own source files. The user wants both machines pointed at the
2691	          same archive, and these are the files that say where it is.
2692	        - The repository files serving the approved installs, from each package's own
2693	          `_OriginPlan` (ruling 4). Nothing else makes a repository travel: one that feeds
2694	          no package this run syncs stays where it is.
2695	
2696	        Only files the target lacks or holds different bytes for are listed — an identical
2697	        file needs no write and can therefore fail nothing. `_package_derived_dests` records
2698	        which packages each write serves, because a derived write has no item of its own to
2699	        fail (D-39) and must charge its failure to the packages that needed it.
2700	        """
2701	        self._failed_derived_writes = {}
2702	        self._package_derived_dests = {}
2703	
2704	        def differs(source_digests: Mapping[str, str], target_digests: Mapping[str, str], filename: str) -> bool:
2705	            return target_digests.get(filename) != source_digests[filename]
2706	
2707	        self._derived_pin_writes = tuple(
2708	            f"{_APT_PREFERENCES_DIR}/{filename}"
2709	            for filename in sorted(self._source_pin_digests)
2710	            if differs(self._source_pin_digests, self._target_pin_digests, filename)
2711	        )
2712	
2713	        # A conflict the user declined is a file this run may NOT write (ruling 6). It is
2714	        # seeded as a failed derived write rather than merely dropped, because a package
2715	        # whose origin depended on it cannot be delivered and installing it anyway would put
2716	        # the wrong vendor's software on the target — the one outcome D-34 exists to prevent.
2717	        skipped = {
2718	            _source_file_destination(filename): (
2719	                "the user chose to keep the target's version of this file for now (ADR-020 D-37)"
2720	            )
2721	            for filename in self._repo_conflicts
2722	            if outcome.decisions.get(f"{_CONFLICT_ID_PREFIX}{filename}") != Decision.APPLY
2723	        }
2724	        self._failed_derived_writes = dict(skipped)
2725	
2726	        distro: list[str] = [
2727	            f"{_APT_SOURCES_DIR}/{filename}"
2728	            for filename in sorted(
2729	                (_DISTRO_SOURCE_FILENAMES - self._withheld_esm_sources) & frozenset(self._source_source_digests)
2730	            )
2731	            if differs(self._source_source_digests, self._target_source_digests, filename)
2732	        ]
2733	        if (
2734	            self._source_sources_list_digest is not None
2735	            and self._source_sources_list_digest != self._target_sources_list_digest
2736	        ):
2737	            distro.append(_APT_SOURCES_LIST)
2738	        self._derived_distro_writes = tuple(dest for dest in distro if dest not in skipped)
2739	
2740	        repo: set[str] = {
2741	            _source_file_destination(filename)
2742	            for filename in self._repo_conflicts
2743	            if outcome.decisions.get(f"{_CONFLICT_ID_PREFIX}{filename}") == Decision.APPLY
2744	        }
2745	        for diff in plan.diffs:
2746	            if diff.item_class is not ItemClass.APT_PACKAGE or diff.action is not DiffAction.INSTALL:
2747	                continue
2748	            if outcome.decisions.get(diff.item_id) != Decision.APPLY:
2749	                continue
2750	            origin_plan = self._origin_plan.get(diff.item_id)
2751	            if origin_plan is None:

2754	            # asymmetry IS D-39's rule: the package still depended on the file.

2756	                _source_file_destination(filename)
2757	                for filename in origin_plan.derived_files
2758	                if self._target_source_digests.get(filename) != self._source_source_digests.get(filename)
2759	            }
2760	            if needed:
2761	                repo.update(needed)
2762	                self._package_derived_dests[diff.item_id] = frozenset(needed)

1	"""`flatpak_sync`: flatpak ref/remote convergence with scope as identity (D-06, D-14,
2	D-29, ADR-020).
3	
4	Scope (user vs. system) is part of a flatpak item's identity, not just a field on it:
5	this project's own reference machine has several runtimes installed in BOTH scopes
6	under the same application id, and `FlatpakItem.item_id`/`FlatpakRemoteItem.item_id`
7	already fold scope into the identity string (`FlatpakItem` below). That is what makes
8	"same application, different scope" fall out of the generic source-vs-target diff as
9	two independent items with no special-casing in this module — a ref present as
10	`user` on the source and `system` on the target produces one install diff and one
11	removal diff, never a single in-place change, because they are simply two different
12	`item_id`s. Normalising that scope split across a machine's own two installations is
13	explicitly out of scope (deferred, CONTEXT.md): it is a change to the machines, not a
14	sync feature, and this job reports the split exactly as found.
15	
16	BRANCH is identity for the same reason (`FlatpakItem`): a ref is identified by its full
17	`<application>/<arch>/<branch>` ref, which is also the only string `flatpak install` and
18	`flatpak uninstall` can resolve on a remote or a machine holding two branches of one
19	application id. Origin is deliberately NOT identity — see `FlatpakItem` for why the two
20	go opposite ways.
21	
22	A remote is DERIVED from the refs approved from it, never ticked (ADR-020 D-41, which is
23	D-37's rule for apt repositories in a second ecosystem). `flatpak install` refuses outright when
24	the remote it names is not configured in the scope being installed into (D-14), so
25	"ref ticked, its remote unticked" was an unrepresentable pairing offered as two independent
26	review lines — and worse, "ref ticked, its remote's URL change declined" silently installed
27	another vendor's build. `accept_review()` therefore turns the approved ref installs into
28	the set of remotes this run must provision (`_derive_remotes`), and `apply()` writes them
29	before the base converge loop reaches the first ref. A remote the source has that feeds no
30	ref approved this run does not travel; there is no flatpak counterpart to apt's
31	never-removed distribution sources, because a fresh flatpak install configures ZERO remotes
32	and a machine with none is a perfectly ordinary machine (measured), so even Flathub travels
33	only as a consequence of something needing it. A derived write has no item of its own, so a
34	failure is recorded against the remote and charged to every approved ref that depended on
35	it (D-39). Only the REMOVAL direction stays a review line, and it takes two answers rather
36	than three (`REPO_REMOVAL_REVIEW_ACTION`): a permanent machine-local mark on a remote whose
37	whole purpose is to feed refs would silently and permanently change where those refs come
38	from, and the remedy is consolidating the two configurations, not recording a preference.
39	
40	Repointing a remote is silent too, with ADR-020 D-41's single exception, which this job
41	applies to remotes exactly as `apt_sync` applies D-37's to repository files: a remote whose URL
42	or verification setting differs is overwritten without a word UNLESS a ref the TARGET
43	recorded skip-always takes it as its origin, in which case both configurations are shown and
44	the answer is overwrite or skip-once (`_capture_remote_conflicts`,
45	`REPO_CONFLICT_REVIEW_ACTION`). Machine-specific is the trigger, not target-only: a
46	skip-always ref is structurally invisible — `filter_inert` keeps it out of the manifest, so
47	it produces no diff in any run — and repointing the remote it updates from moves software
48	the user explicitly told this tool to leave alone. Two answers, nothing recorded. A skipped
49	conflict keeps the remote out of the write set but NOT out of the D-39 attribution map, so
50	every approved ref that needed the source's URL fails naming the decision rather than
51	installing from the URL the target still has.
52	
53	Before converging a ref, its origin remote is re-read off the TARGET and required to carry
54	the source
55	remote's URL and verification setting — not merely to exist under the same name
56	(`_origin_refusal`), because a same-named remote pointing elsewhere serves a different
57	vendor's build of the same ref at exit 0 with no warning; and after the install the ref's
58	own reported origin is read back and resolved to a URL again (`_installed_origin_refusal`),
59	so the guarantee is checked rather than inferred. Either refusal is a per-item failure
60	naming both URLs, never an install issued in hope (T-02-24). That same read is what checks
61	the derived writes actually landed: `flatpak remote-add --if-not-exists <name> <other url>`
62	exits 0 and changes nothing (measured), so the write's exit code proves nothing and only
63	the target's own answer does.
64	
65	The removal direction is disclosure rather than refusal (#214): a remote offered for
66	deletion carries, in its review `detail`, the target refs that still name it as their
67	origin in that same scope — deleting a remote whose refs are being removed too is
68	legitimate cleanup, so the decision stays in the review where D-30 puts apt's collateral:
69	the dependent refs are known from the plan's own reads, so the consequence can be stated
70	while the user is deciding about the deletion that causes it.
71	
72	A remote carries its TRUST as part of the item, not as a property of the machine that
73	happens to hold it (#215): `FlatpakRemoteItem` records the remote's GPG-verification
74	setting and the digest of its own ostree keyring, and convergence replicates both —
75	`flatpak remote-add --gpg-import=<staged key>` for a signed remote, `--no-gpg-verify`
76	only when the SOURCE remote is itself unverified. Without this a replicated remote is
77	configured but unusable: flatpak refuses every install from it with `Can't check
78	signature: public key not found`. The key bytes travel byte-for-byte from the source
79	machine and are never re-fetched from a vendor (ADR-020 D-12's rule for apt signing
80	keys), staged under the target's `~/.cache/pc-switcher/` exactly as `apt_sync` stages
81	`/etc/apt` content, because SFTP reaches only the SSH user's own home.
82	
83	The flatpak OSTree store stays authoritative for its own state (D-01): this job never
84	WRITES into `/var/lib/flatpak` or `~/.local/share/flatpak`, only shells out to `flatpak`
85	itself. It does READ one file there, `<installation>/repo/<remote>.trustedkeys.gpg`,
86	because no flatpak command prints or exports a remote's key and libostree's own CLI is
87	not installed alongside flatpak on Ubuntu. `flatpak_sync_exclude_paths()` exports
88	`~/.local/share/flatpak` so `folder_sync` stops mirroring the store this job owns
89	(D-29, ADR-018) — but NOT `~/.var/app`, which is per-application USER DATA that stays
90	folder_sync's territory;
91	D-17's job-before-folder_sync ordering exists precisely so `flatpak install` creates
92	the store first and folder_sync's data lands on top of it, never the reverse.
93	
94	`FlatpakSyncJob` subclasses `PackageSyncJob` and implements the abstract `plan()`, for the
95	same reason `SnapSyncJob` does: what a diff even IS differs per manager, so the base class
96	holds no diff to inherit. apt's own diff is apt-package-shaped — one item class,
97	`MISSING_ON_TARGET`/`EXTRA_ON_TARGET`/`VERSION_MISMATCH` only, no notion of derived work
98	that must land ahead of an item. `plan()` here reuses every manager-agnostic building
99	block the shared core provides — `DecisionFile`/`filter_inert` (D-08's machine-local
100	skip-always filtering) and `PackageSyncJob._build_review_groups` (D-24's action-grouped
101	review) — so only capture, diff and converge are genuinely flatpak-specific.
102	`accept_review()` is overridden to turn the approved refs into the derived remote set,
103	and `apply()` to write those remotes before the base converge loop reaches its first ref.
104	`execute()` is inherited unchanged and is where this job's own single review happens,
105	before its own first mutating command: there is no coordinator and no review spanning two
106	managers (D-15, D-24).
107	
108	Flatpak ref VERSIONS are captured for reporting only (D-04, like apt package
109	versions): a version difference on a ref present in the same scope on both machines
110	is a `REPORT_ONLY` diff, never something this job installs or removes to force.
111	
112	A ref's ORIGIN is reported the same way and outranks it (`_diff_flatpak_refs`, D-41). The
113	two install-time refusals above guard an install, and a ref already present on BOTH machines
114	issues none — so the already-diverged case they cannot see is `ORIGIN_MISMATCH`: same scope,
115	same `<application>/<arch>/<branch>`, two vendors. It is compared by the remotes' URLs rather
116	than their names for the reason `5fc3ac01` records, so a target `flathub` pointing at the beta
117	repo is caught and a remote the two machines merely named differently is not. It is
118	`REPORT_ONLY` because flatpak leaves no verb: `flatpak install <other remote> <installed ref>`
119	refuses with `already installed from remote <name>` (measured), so converging it would mean
120	uninstalling the app the user has and reinstalling it from the other vendor.
121	"""

282	# item or writes the orphaned-refs detail.

285	@dataclass(frozen=True)
286	class FlatpakItem:
287	    """One installed flatpak application ref (D-06), scoped user or system.
288	
289	    `scope` lives inside the identity string, not just as a field: this project's own
290	    machine has several runtimes installed in both scopes with the same application
291	    id, and folding scope into `item_id` is what makes "same name, different scope"
292	    fall out of the generic diff engine as two distinct items with no special-casing
293	    in `flatpak_sync`.
294	
295	    So does `ref` (`<application>/<arch>/<branch>`), and NOT the bare application id, for
296	    two reasons that the application id alone cannot serve:
297	
298	    - Two branches of one application id can be installed side by side in ONE scope —
299	      that is what branches are for — so `(scope, application)` is not a unique key for a
300	      machine's own listing, and keying on it silently drops one of the two rows when the
301	      captured items are folded into a `{item_id: item}` map.
302	    - The install and the removal both need the full ref anyway (`_FLATPAK_LIST_CMD`), so
303	      the identity and the command argument are the same string rather than two facts that
304	      can drift.
305	
306	    ORIGIN deliberately stays out (a field, not identity), because the install-plus-removal
307	    pair it would produce cannot converge: `flatpak install <other remote> <ref>` on an
308	    already-installed ref exits with `<ref> is already installed from remote <name>`, so
309	    the install half could never run while the removal half proposed deleting the app the
310	    user has. A BRANCH difference has the opposite property — branches coexist, so the
311	    install half succeeds and the removal half then leaves exactly the source's set — which
312	    is why a branch change replicates as two items and an origin change does not.
313	    """
314	
315	    application: str
316	    version: str
317	    origin: str
318	    scope: Literal["user", "system"]
319	    ref: str
320	
321	    ITEM_CLASS: ClassVar[ItemClass] = ItemClass.FLATPAK_REF
322	
323	    @property
324	    def item_id(self) -> str:
325	        """Stable identity string: `flatpak:ref:<scope>:<application>/<arch>/<branch>`."""
326	        return f"flatpak:ref:{self.scope}:{self.ref}"
327	
328	    def label(self) -> str:
329	        """Human-readable text for the review UI and logs."""
330	        return f"{self.ref} ({self.version}, {self.origin}, {self.scope})"
331

333	@dataclass(frozen=True)
334	class FlatpakRemoteItem:
335	    """One configured flatpak remote (D-11/D-14), scoped user or system.
336	
337	    Flatpak tracks remotes per-installation: `flathub` commonly exists in both scopes
338	    with a byte-identical URL, yet the two are separate configuration the target must
339	    provision separately. `scope` inside `item_id` (same reasoning as `FlatpakItem`)
340	    is what keeps those two facts distinct rather than colliding on the shared name.
341	
342	    `gpg_verify` and `key_digest` are the remote's TRUST configuration (#215). A remote
343	    replicated as name+url alone is configured but unusable — flatpak refuses every
344	    install from it with `Can't check signature: public key not found` — so trust is
345	    part of the item, not an incidental of the machine. `gpg_verify` is read from
346	    `flatpak remotes --columns=options` (the `no-gpg-verify` token) and `key_digest` is
347	    the sha256 of the remote's own ostree keyring, `<installation>/repo/<name>.
348	    trustedkeys.gpg`; it is `None` for an unverified remote and for a verified one whose
349	    trust comes from a machine-level anchor under `/usr/share/ostree/trusted.gpg.d`
350	    rather than from a per-remote key.
351	
352	    The DIGEST lives on the item, not the key bytes. An item is carried through the diff,
353	    the review and the decision file, all of which want an identity and a comparison,
354	    never a payload; the bytes themselves travel
355	    separately and byte-for-byte (`flatpak_sync` stages the source's keyring file and
356	    passes it to `flatpak remote-add --gpg-import`), which is ADR-020 D-12's rule that
357	    key material is copied from the source machine and never re-fetched from a vendor.
358	    """
359	
360	    name: str
361	    url: str
362	    scope: Literal["user", "system"]
363	    gpg_verify: bool = True
364	    key_digest: str | None = None
365	    # Whether the source's remote carries a ref filter, for the warning `apply()` raises per
366	    # derived remote (ADR-020, Consequences). Deliberately `compare=False`, which is what
367	    # keeps it a REPORTED fact rather than a converged one: the filter's content lives at an
368	    # arbitrary local path outside the ostree store (`_FILTERED_OPTION`), so no command this
369	    # job can issue would make the two sides agree — and letting it into `__eq__` would make
370	    # `_write_derived_remote`'s whole-item equality test miss, issuing a `remote-modify` that
371	    # changes nothing and leaves the difference exactly where it was, every run.
372	    is_filtered: bool = field(default=False, compare=False)
373	
374	    ITEM_CLASS: ClassVar[ItemClass] = ItemClass.FLATPAK_REMOTE
375	
376	    @property
377	    def item_id(self) -> str:
378	        """Stable identity string: `flatpak:remote:<scope>:<name>`."""
379	        return f"flatpak:remote:{self.scope}:{self.name}"
380	
381	    def label(self) -> str:
382	        """Human-readable text for the review UI and logs."""
383	        return f"{self.name} remote ({self.scope}): {self.url}"

467	    """`sudo ` for a system-scope converge command, empty for user-scope (T-02-23,

476	def _repo_dir_expression(scope: str) -> str:
477	    """The scope's ostree repo directory, as a SHELL EXPRESSION for `run_command`.
478	
479	    `$HOME` is left for the remote shell to expand rather than resolved here: the user
480	    installation lives under the invoking user's own home on each machine, and the two
481	    machines' usernames differ. Both ends therefore compute the same relative location
482	    (`~/.local/share/flatpak`, the very path `flatpak_sync_exclude_paths()` already
483	    claims) in their own environment. `$XDG_DATA_HOME` is deliberately NOT consulted: it
484	    is typically set in a desktop session and unset over a non-interactive SSH exec
485	    channel, so honouring it would make the source and the target disagree about where
486	    the same user's remotes live and manufacture a phantom key diff.
487	    """
488	    if scope == "system":
489	        return f"{_FLATPAK_SYSTEM_INSTALLATION}/repo"
490	    return f"$HOME/{_FLATPAK_DATA_RELPATH}/repo"
491

499	def _source_keyring_path(item: FlatpakRemoteItem) -> Path:
500	    """The LOCAL path of the source machine's own keyring file for `item`.
501	
502	    `send_file` transfers from the local filesystem, and the source executor runs on
503	    this machine as this user (the same assumption `AptSyncJob._write_or_remove_repo_item`
504	    makes for `/etc/apt`), so `Path.home()` resolves the very directory
505	    `_repo_dir_expression("user")`'s `$HOME` expands to on the source side.
506	    """
507	    installation = _FLATPAK_SYSTEM_INSTALLATION if item.scope == "system" else Path.home() / _FLATPAK_DATA_RELPATH
508	    return installation / "repo" / f"{item.name}{_TRUSTEDKEYS_SUFFIX}"

511	def _parse_keyring_digests(output: str) -> dict[str, str]:
512	    """`{remote name: sha256}` from one scope's batched `sha256sum` output.
513	
514	    `<digest>  <path>` lines, mapped by stripping the `.trustedkeys.gpg` suffix off the
515	    basename — a remote name may contain dots (`my.remote.name.trustedkeys.gpg`,
516	    verified live), so only the fixed suffix is removed, never everything after the
517	    first dot.
518	    """
519	    digests: dict[str, str] = {}
520	    for line in _lines(output):
521	        parts = line.split(maxsplit=1)
522	        if len(parts) != 2:
523	            continue
524	        digest, path = parts
525	        name = Path(path.strip()).name
526	        if not name.endswith(_TRUSTEDKEYS_SUFFIX):
527	            continue
528	        digests[name[: -len(_TRUSTEDKEYS_SUFFIX)]] = digest
529	    return digests

532	def _split_flatpak_item_id(item_id: str, expected_kind: Literal["ref", "remote", "mask"]) -> tuple[str, str]:
533	    """`(scope, name)` from a `flatpak:<kind>:<scope>:<name>` item id (`FlatpakItem` above).
534	
535	    `name` is the full `<application>/<arch>/<branch>` ref for a ref, the remote name for
536	    a remote, the pattern for a mask — none carries a `:` of its own: application ids and
537	    remote names are dotted/alnum tokens, and refs and mask patterns are partial refs with
538	    `/` and `*` but never `:` (RESEARCH Standard Stack, verified live), so a fixed 3-colon
539	    split is exact rather than a heuristic (the `split(":", 3)` cap keeps every `/` intact).
540	    This is a legitimate use of a
541	    stable identity string (the same pattern `apt_sync._package_name` and
542	    `snap_sync._snap_name` already establish): the plan only ever carries `ItemDiff`s,
543	    not the richer item dataclasses, so converge() recovers scope/name from the id.
544	    """
545	    parts = item_id.split(":", 3)
546	    if len(parts) != 4 or parts[0] != "flatpak" or parts[1] != expected_kind:
547	        raise ValueError(f"not a flatpak {expected_kind} item id: {item_id!r}")
548	    _, _, scope, name = parts
549	    return scope, name

552	def _parse_flatpak_list(output: str) -> list[FlatpakItem]:
553	    """Parse `_FLATPAK_LIST_CMD`'s tab-separated output into `FlatpakItem`s.
554	
555	    A line whose `installation` field is neither `user` nor `system` (flatpak permits
556	    additional named installations beyond the two this item model represents) is
557	    skipped rather than guessed at — this project's own machines only ever use the
558	    two standard scopes (CONTEXT.md's live inventory), and a third would need its own
559	    modelling decision, not a silent default.
560	    """
561	    items: list[FlatpakItem] = []
562	    for line in _lines(output):
563	        fields = line.split("\t")
564	        if len(fields) != 5:
565	            continue
566	        application, version, origin, installation, ref = fields
567	        scope: Literal["user", "system"]
568	        if installation == "user":
569	            scope = "user"
570	        elif installation == "system":
571	            scope = "system"
572	        else:
573	            continue
574	        items.append(FlatpakItem(application=application, version=version, origin=origin, scope=scope, ref=ref))
575	    return items

578	def _parse_flatpak_remotes(
579	    output: str, scope: Literal["user", "system"], key_digests: Mapping[str, str]
580	) -> list[FlatpakRemoteItem]:
581	    """Parse one scope's `flatpak remotes --columns=name,url,options` output.
582	
583	    `scope` is a parameter, not a parsed column: unlike `flatpak list`, this command
584	    has no scope column of its own — the caller already knows which scope it asked
585	    about, because it chose the `--user`/`--system` flag (module docstring).
586	    `key_digests` is the same scope's `_parse_keyring_digests` map, joined here by
587	    remote name so a remote's trust arrives as part of the item rather than as a
588	    second lookup at converge time (#215).
589	
590	    `options` is a comma-separated token list carrying two facts this job reads: whether
591	    verification is off (`no-gpg-verify`) and whether the remote carries a ref filter
592	    (`filtered`, `_FILTERED_OPTION`). They are independent tokens, so a filtered remote's
593	    verification state parses exactly as an unfiltered one's.
594	
595	    A remote with no options at all prints only two fields (no trailing tab), so both
596	    widths are accepted; a remote absent from `key_digests` keeps `key_digest=None`,
597	    which is the honest reading of "verification is on but this remote carries no key of
598	    its own" — trust then comes from a machine-level anchor this job neither reads nor
599	    replicates.
600	    """
601	    items: list[FlatpakRemoteItem] = []
602	    for line in _lines(output):
603	        fields = line.split("\t")
604	        if len(fields) not in (2, 3):
605	            continue
606	        name, url = fields[0], fields[1]
607	        options = fields[2].split(",") if len(fields) == 3 else []
608	        gpg_verify = _NO_GPG_VERIFY_OPTION not in options
609	        items.append(
610	            FlatpakRemoteItem(
611	                name=name,
612	                url=url,
613	                scope=scope,
614	                gpg_verify=gpg_verify,
615	                key_digest=key_digests.get(name) if gpg_verify else None,
616	                is_filtered=_FILTERED_OPTION in options,
617	            )
618	        )
619	    return items

622	def _parse_flatpak_masks(output: str, scope: Literal["user", "system"]) -> list[FlatpakMaskItem]:
623	    """Parse one scope's `flatpak {--user|--system} mask` output into `FlatpakMaskItem`s.
624	
625	    Unlike the tab-separated list commands, `flatpak mask` prints each pattern on its
626	    own line prefixed with two leading spaces and no header (RESEARCH: verified live,
627	    Flatpak 1.14.6), so this strips leading/trailing whitespace per non-blank line
628	    rather than splitting on tabs. `scope` is a parameter, not a parsed column: the
629	    command has no scope column: the caller already chose the `--user`/`--system` flag
630	    (same reasoning as `_parse_flatpak_remotes`).
631	    """
632	    items: list[FlatpakMaskItem] = []

634	        pattern = line.strip()
635	        if not pattern:
636	            continue
637	        items.append(FlatpakMaskItem(pattern=pattern, scope=scope))
638	    return items

710	def _same_vendor(
711	    source_item: FlatpakItem,
712	    target_item: FlatpakItem,
713	    source_remote_urls: Mapping[tuple[str, str], str],
714	    target_remote_urls: Mapping[tuple[str, str], str],
715	) -> bool:
716	    """Whether the two machines' copies of one ref provably come from the same vendor.
717	
718	    ADR-020 D-41: origin is compared by the remote's URL, never by its name. Both directions
719	    of that rule matter here and pull opposite ways, which is why neither comparison alone is
720	    the answer:
721	
722	    - Same NAME, different URL is the dangerous case — a target remote called `flathub`
723	      pointing at the beta repo serves a different vendor's build and `flatpak list
724	      --columns=origin` prints `flathub` on both machines (measured, `5fc3ac01`). Comparing
725	      names would report nothing at all.
726	    - Different NAME, same URL is a pure rename. The provenance is identical, so reporting it
727	      would be noise about a label.
728	
729	    When either side's origin resolves to no configured remote — the machine holds a ref whose
730	    remote has since been deleted — there is no URL to compare and the fallback is the name.
731	    That is the conservative reading: it keeps an ordinary machine quiet on the equal-name case
732	    rather than manufacturing a mismatch out of a lookup miss, and still reports two different
733	    names, which is all the evidence there is.
734	    """
735	    source_url = source_remote_urls.get((source_item.scope, source_item.origin))
736	    target_url = target_remote_urls.get((target_item.scope, target_item.origin))
737	    if source_url is not None and target_url is not None:
738	        return source_url == target_url
739	    return source_item.origin == target_item.origin

742	def _diff_flatpak_refs(
743	    source_items: Sequence[FlatpakItem],
744	    target_items: Sequence[FlatpakItem],
745	    source_remote_urls: Mapping[tuple[str, str], str],
746	    target_remote_urls: Mapping[tuple[str, str], str],
747	) -> list[ItemDiff]:
748	    """One diff per ref `item_id` present on either side, source-then-target order —
749	    same shape as `PackageSyncJob._diff_apt_packages`/`snap_sync._diff_snap_items`.
750	    Scope already lives inside `item_id`, so an application installed in a different
751	    scope on each machine naturally produces one install-side entry and one
752	    remove-side entry here, never a single combined diff.
753	
754	    Present on both, the origin comparison runs BEFORE the version comparison, exactly as
755	    `_diff_apt_packages` orders its own two provenance-and-version branches: two vendors'
756	    builds of one ref share no version scale — Flathub's and Flathub-beta's `org.mozilla.
757	    firefox` are numbered independently — so reporting "source has X, target has Y" would
758	    state a difference of degree where the real difference is of provenance, and would hide
759	    the wrong-vendor finding behind a version line the user reads as ordinary drift.
760	    """

837	def _derive_remotes(
838	    approved_ref_ids: frozenset[str],
839	    source_refs_by_id: Mapping[str, FlatpakItem],
840	    source_ref_origins: Mapping[tuple[str, str], str],
841	    source_runtime_by_ref_id: Mapping[str, str],
842	) -> tuple[tuple[_DerivedRemote, ...], dict[str, frozenset[str]]]:
843	    """`(remotes to provision, {approved ref item_id: the remote_ids it depends on})`.
844	
845	    Two sources feed the set, both computed from facts `plan()` already read off the source
846	    and neither costing a command here:
847	
848	    - the approved ref's own origin, and
849	    - the origin of the runtime that ref is built against, because `flatpak install` pulls
850	      the runtime too and resolves it from whatever remotes are configured — an app on
851	      remote X built against a runtime the source holds from remote Y would otherwise be
852	      approved with only X provisioned.
853	
854	    The runtime is looked up in EITHER scope on the source (a user app against a
855	    system-installed runtime is the ordinary case) but its remote is always derived in the
856	    APP's scope, because that is the installation the target may have to pull the runtime
857	    into. Deriving one remote too many in the rare cross-scope case costs a
858	    `flatpak remote-add`; deriving one too few costs the install.
859	
860	    The attribution map is D-39's: a derived write has no item to fail, so it fails every
861	    approved ref that named it.
862	    """
863	    derived: dict[str, _DerivedRemote] = {}
864	    depends_on: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
865	
866	    def need(item_id: str, scope: Literal["user", "system"], name: str, reason: str) -> None:
867	        remote_id = f"flatpak:remote:{scope}:{name}"
868	        derived.setdefault(
869	            remote_id,
870	            _DerivedRemote(
871	                remote_id=remote_id,
872	                scope=scope,
873	                name=name,
874	                reason="ref_origin" if reason == "ref_origin" else "runtime_origin",
875	            ),
876	        )
877	        depends_on.setdefault(item_id, set()).add(remote_id)
878	
879	    for item_id in sorted(approved_ref_ids):
880	        item = source_refs_by_id.get(item_id)
881	        if item is None:
882	            continue
883	        need(item_id, item.scope, item.origin, "ref_origin")
884	        runtime = source_runtime_by_ref_id.get(item_id)
885	        if runtime is None:
886	            continue
887	        other_scope = "system" if item.scope == "user" else "user"
888	        runtime_origin = source_ref_origins.get((item.scope, runtime)) or source_ref_origins.get(
889	            (other_scope, runtime)
890	        )
891	        if runtime_origin is not None:
892	            need(item_id, item.scope, runtime_origin, "runtime_origin")
893	
894	    return (
895	        tuple(derived[remote_id] for remote_id in sorted(derived)),
896	        {item_id: frozenset(remote_ids) for item_id, remote_ids in depends_on.items()},
897	    )

987	def _remote_trust_flags(item: FlatpakRemoteItem, staged_key: str | None, *, restore_verification: bool) -> str:
988	    """The `flatpak remote-add`/`remote-modify` flags that replicate `item`'s trust
989	    (#215), as a string that begins with a space or is empty.
990	
991	    `--no-gpg-verify` is emitted if and only if the SOURCE remote is itself unverified:
992	    a remote the source verifies can never be silently downgraded on the target, and an
993	    unverified one is replicated as unverified rather than as a verified remote that
994	    would then refuse every install. `restore_verification` adds the explicit
995	    `--gpg-verify` that only `remote-modify` accepts (`remote-add` has no such flag —
996	    verification is its default), so a CHANGE can lift a target-side remote back out of
997	    `no-gpg-verify` instead of leaving the divergence half-converged.
998	
999	    A verified remote with `staged_key is None` carries no per-remote key at all: nothing
1000	    is invented for it, and its trust stays whatever machine-level anchor the target has.
1001	    """
1002	    if not item.gpg_verify:
1003	        return " --no-gpg-verify"
1004	    flags = " --gpg-verify" if restore_verification else ""
1005	    if staged_key is not None:
1006	        flags += f" --gpg-import={shlex.quote(staged_key)}"
1007	    return flags

1922	    async def _origin_refusal(self, scope: str, origin: str) -> str | None:
1923	        """`None` if a ref may be installed from `origin` in `scope`, otherwise why not.
1924	
1925	        Name equality is NOT the test, and that is the whole point of this guard. Measured
1926	        against real Flathub: a target remote called `flathub` pointing at
1927	        `https://dl.flathub.org/beta-repo/` serves a DIFFERENT vendor's build of the same
1928	        ref — different commit, different collection id, different binary — and
1929	        `flatpak install --assumeyes flathub <ref>` installs it at exit 0 with no warning,
1930	        while `flatpak list --columns=origin` reports `flathub` on both machines. Only the
1931	        URL separates the two, so the URL is what is compared (ADR-020 D-41: an origin is
1932	        a remote's URL, never its name).
1933	
1934	        GPG verification is compared too: a ref the source takes from a verified remote,
1935	        landing on the target from an unverified one of the same name, has not replicated
1936	        its provenance either. The per-remote KEY DIGEST deliberately is not — ostree's
1937	        import merges rather than replaces, so a target that already trusted another key
1938	        for this remote keeps both digests unequal forever, and refusing on that would
1939	        refuse every install from it for good.
1940	        """
1941	        remote_id = f"flatpak:remote:{scope}:{origin}"
1942	        source_remote = self._source_remotes_by_id.get(remote_id)
1943	        if source_remote is None:
1944	            return (
1945	                f"the source has no {scope}-scope remote named {origin!r}, so the ref's own origin "
1946	                "cannot be replicated (ADR-020 D-41)"
1947	            )
1948	        target_remote = (await self._target_remotes_now()).get(remote_id)
1949	        if target_remote is None:
1950	            return f"origin remote {origin!r} ({scope}) is not configured on the target (D-14)"
1951	        if target_remote.url != source_remote.url:
1952	            return (
1953	                f"the target's {scope}-scope remote {origin!r} points at {target_remote.url}, "
1954	                f"but the source takes this ref from {source_remote.url} — same name, different "
1955	                "repository, so installing would replicate the name and invert the provenance"
1956	            )
1957	        if target_remote.gpg_verify != source_remote.gpg_verify:
1958	            return (
1959	                f"the target's {scope}-scope remote {origin!r} has gpg verification "
1960	                f"{_verification_word(target_remote)} while the source's has it "
1961	                f"{_verification_word(source_remote)}"
1962	            )
1963	        return None

1965	    async def _installed_origin_refusal(self, scope: str, ref: str, expected_origin: str) -> str | None:
